title: Analysis of Parameters on the Phase Distribution of Debris Clouds in Hypervelocity Impacts
abstract: The phase distribution is a crucial aspect of the debris cloud’s characteristics. Solid-phase fragments maintain material strength and demonstrate superior penetration capabilities, whereas liquid- and gas-phase debris exhibit reduced penetration efficiency but still impose momentum and thermal impact on the rear plate. In this study, the influences of impact velocity v , projectile diameter D , and thickness-to-diameter ratio h / D on the phase distribution were discussed. The results of the orthogonal test indicated that v importantly affected the phase distribution. h / D had a certain influence on phase distribution, although its influence was smaller than that of velocity. Projectile diameter had a minimal effect on the solid phase but did have some effect on the melting and liquid phase. Empirical formulas were derived for h / D and v . Additionally, the phase space was defined and the secondary phase transition of the debris cloud impacting the rear plate was discussed.

title: Programmable Shape Morphing and Space Deployment through Graded Derivatives of Origami Architectures
abstract: Real-time programmable mechanical features including shape-morphing ability in metamaterials and metasurfaces can be crucial for a range of technologically demanding space applications such as deployable space structures and antennas, adaptive solar arrays, robotic arms, actuators, and advanced robotic materials. This paper proposes second-order derivatives of spatially varying Miura-based origami architectures like graded Arc Miura, inclined Arc Miura, and tapered Arc Miura for achieving a range of programmable shape-changing capabilities. The rigid foldability and motion behavior of the graded geometries are investigated thoroughly based on computational simulations and tabletop experiments using physical prototypes, leading to the evidence of on-demand shape morphing and target curvature attainment under limited actuation, and transitional deployment from 2-dimensional to 3-dimensional states. An efficient approach of kinematic mapping is developed based on idealized spherical 4R linkages involving Denavit–Hartenberg matrix notations, resulting in piecewise spatially graded tessellations for achieving programmed pre-defined symmetric and asymmetric curvatures with complex 2- and 3-dimensional geometrical shapes. The fundamental mechanics of the proposed origami metamaterials being mostly scale independent, this emerging class of deployable shape-changing architectures can be directly transferred for application in a range of millimeter-, micrometer-, and nanometer-size space systems, essentially opening avenues for the design of various programmable structures and machines at multiple length scales.

title: Online Threshold Voltage Monitoring for Silicon Carbide Planar and Trench MOSFETs under γ-Ray Exposure
abstract: Traditional threshold-voltage ( V th ) measurements are usually performed either offline or during in situ state monitoring, are typically conducted offline or in situ state monitoring, limiting their ability to assess V th accurately during the aging process. This paper proposes an online method to monitor the V th of silicon carbide (SiC) metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs) within the space environment characterized by high-energy ionizing radiation. After observing the V th degradation during the experimental procedure, we simulated the total ionizing dose (TID)-induced degradation to validate the sampled V th of our experiment. The study also predicts V th degradation trends by analyzing the mechanisms of TID-induced degradation. A comprehensive 5-h TID experiment was performed using monitoring methods on a γ-ray plane at a dose rate of 50 rad(Si)/s, provided by a Co-60 source. V th measurements for planar MOSFETs and trench MOSFETs were collected every 15 min with a sampling accuracy of 0.1 V. The monitoring results aligned closely with the predicted trends. To further verify the efficacy of the monitoring technology, technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations were conducted to assess the V th sensitivity to TID. The proposed monitoring technology offers adjustable sampling accuracy and frequency, high precision, and a broad sampling range, making it suitable for most reliability test online monitoring applications. This method provides valuable insights for predicting the end-of-life and ensuring the space reliability of SiC MOSFETs.

title: Detection of Earth’s Free Oscillations Utilizing TianQin
abstract: The measurement of Earth’s free oscillations plays an important role in studying Earth’s large-scale structure. Space technology development presents a potential method to observe these normal modes by measuring intersatellite distances. However, the disturbance from Earth’s low-degree gravity field makes it challenging for low Earth orbit gravity measurement satellites such as Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment and TianQin-2 to extract signals from Earth’s free oscillations directly. Here, we propose that by taking advantage of the high Earth orbit, the TianQin satellites can effectively avoid this disturbance, enabling direct measurement of Earth’s free oscillations. We derive an analytical waveform to describe the response of Earth’s free oscillations in TianQin. Based on this waveform, we use Bayesian analysis to extract the normal modes from numerical simulation data and perform parameter estimation. Our findings reveal that for a magnitude 7.9, Wenchuan-like earthquake, the resulting free oscillations will generate a signal with a signal-to-noise ratio of 73 in TianQin, and approximately 9 different modes can be distinguished. This result shows that TianQin can open a new window to examine Earth’s free oscillations and study Earth’s interior and earthquakes independently from ground-based gravity measurement.

title: Power Optimization and Control for ELITE Based on Robust PWA Multiplexed MPC and Differential Evolution
abstract: The extremely low Earth imaging and technology explorer (ELITE), a very low Earth orbit (VLEO) satellite, is expected to face increasingly high-power demands from its electrical propulsion system, due to significant atmospheric drag, and its attitude determination and control system (ADCS), especially during target pointing. This results in significant power-related concerns that have potentially detrimental impacts on the satellite’s mission success. To address these concerns, this paper innovatively proposes power optimization control strategies and algorithms to optimize ELITE’s power generation. The power control strategies are specifically designed for each significant phase of the mission to account for the constraints in the respective phases. The innovatively developed robust piecewise affine multiplexed model predictive control (RPWA MMPC) features a piecewise affine model that breaks down the complex nonlinear dynamics of ELITE into highly accurate linear models, which are further divided into lower dimensional subproblems via the multiplexed feature. This significantly decreases the computational resources required. An observer is also included to account for uncertainties and disturbances for robustness. Meanwhile, differential evolution (DE) has been innovatively integrated into the ADCS to enable the synchronous operations of sun tracking and target pointing, significantly optimizing the power generation of ELITE, potentially marking a breakthrough in the realm of satellite research and development. The efficacy of these strategies and algorithms was validated through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experimentation, proving that with these strategies and algorithms, ELITE’s power system has the capability to meet the large power demands required for the mission, and testifying its potential to revolutionize VLEO remote sensing.

title: The Rectification Mode in a Traveling Wave Tube with High Power and High Efficiency
abstract: The research on high-power and efficient rectification is one of the key and difficult points in microwave energy transmission systems for medium- and long-distance high-power transmission. Traveling wave tube amplification (TWTA) is widely used in wireless signal transmission systems, which is renowned for its high power and high efficiency compared with those of solid-state devices. The rectification mode of TWTA’s energy conversion is firstly reported by resetting the operating parameters without changing the structure. Pierce’s theory is utilized to derive that there are power amplification and rectification modes in the same traveling wave tube structure by using assumed propagation parameters for rectification conditions firstly. The numerical simulation result is in good agreement with the theoretical result. Moreover, it is shown that the power capacity and efficiency of traveling wave tube rectification are almost the same as those of the TWTA of the same traveling wave tube structure. Experimental results of the TWTA product indicate that there is a rectification mode in the same energy conversion structure. At the same power, the rectification efficiency is lower than the amplification efficiency due to the use of an amplification collection stage.

title: Satellite Attitude Anomaly Detection in Ground Data Processing
abstract: In Earth observing satellite data processing, geometric image processing is the first and foremost step in generating accurate data products. The satellite’s attitude plays a crucial role in acquiring planned images, and any anomaly in attitude computation can lead to targeting inaccuracies and image distortion. Existing anomaly detection methods rely heavily on telemetry data and complex machine learning models, making them computationally intensive and less adaptable for real-time applications. In this work, we propose a novel graph-based RANSAC (Random Sample Consensus) algorithm to detect attitude anomalies in satellite profiles, ensuring early detection and correction in the ground data processing chain. Our method segments attitude profiles into structured components, identifies deviations from expected patterns, and estimates the maximum usable attitude range for longer image acquisitions. Unlike traditional approaches, the proposed method is computationally efficient, requires minimal prior knowledge of sensor-specific characteristics, and enables early anomaly flagging with improved reliability. Experimental validation on Cartosat-2S datasets demonstrates that the algorithm successfully identifies anomalous roll, pitch, and yaw profiles, providing insights into their impact on image quality. This approach enhances operational efficiency by reducing data rejection rates and enabling corrective measures before product generation.

title: Detecting Patched Anomaly Regions in Spatial Electric Field Power Spectrum Images
abstract: Research has found patched anomaly regions in the power spectrum images of ionospheric electric fields in space, which are widely distributed. To effectively detect these patched abnormal regions, this paper proposes a new patched abnormal region detection method, KANs-Unet, based on Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KANs) and U-net networks. The model embeds the KAN-Conv convolution module based on KANs in the encoder section, implements learnable activation functions at the network edge, reduces model parameters, and improves the network’s generalization ability. A feature pyramid attention module is introduced at the junction of the encoder and decoder to enhance the model’s ability to capture features of different scales. The convolutional block attention module is introduced in the decoder section, effectively enhancing the network’s attention to valuable features and improving the feature expression ability. The experimental results of patched anomaly detection show that the KANs-Unet algorithm has better detection performance than the currently popular semantic segmentation algorithms. To further study the characteristics of patched anomaly areas and the differences during major geomagnetic storms, in this research work, we analyzed the patched anomaly areas from November 2021 to October 2022 and from 2024 May 1 to 2024 May 13 during major geomagnetic storms. It was found that the majority of the central frequency points in the patched anomaly area are distributed between 3 and 12.5 kHz, and the number of orbits in the patched anomaly area during the 3 seasons of spring, summer, and autumn is higher than that of the descending orbit, except in winter, where the opposite is true. During a major geomagnetic storm, the overall distribution of patched anomaly areas shows a parallel trend with a band-like distribution. The spatial distribution of magnetic latitudes is relatively scattered, especially in the southern hemisphere, where the magnetic latitudes are wider. Additionally, the number of orbits with patched anomaly areas during ascending increases, especially during peak periods of major geomagnetic storms. In addition, the phenomenon of dual events in patched anomaly areas was also discovered, where 2 consecutive patched anomaly areas appear in the same hemisphere.

title: Multiscale Modeling Techniques in the Study of 2-Dimensional Materials under Ionizing Radiation
abstract: Two-dimensional materials (2DMs)-based devices exhibit aerospace potential due to their superior properties. However, the operational reliability of 2DMs-based devices in space environments is significantly influenced by charged-particle radiation, necessitating rigorous ground-based radiation tolerance assessments. Current research on radiation effects in 2DMs is primarily experimental, yet such methodologies are inherently time-consuming, resource-intensive, and limited in throughput. To address these challenges, computational modeling and simulation techniques are increasingly being integrated with experimental characterization to accelerate materials design and unravel underlying physical mechanisms. This review systematically evaluates the state-of-the-art multiscale computational frameworks for 2DMs research, focusing on recent advancements, technical challenges, and emerging opportunities. A novel integrative approach is proposed, combining density functional theory, molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo, finite element analysis, and machine learning techniques. Particular emphasis is placed on addressing challenges in multiscale modeling, including accurate representation of complex phenomena across spatial and temporal scales under extreme environmental conditions. Conversely, opportunities for enhancing predictive capabilities are highlighted, with implications for expediting materials discovery in electronics, photonics, energy storage, catalysis, and nanomechanical systems. This comprehensive survey provides a strategic roadmap for future research directions in multiscale computational modeling of 2DMs, emphasizing interdisciplinary methodologies that bridge atomistic simulations with macroscale engineering applications. The insights presented herein aim to advance the development of radiation-hardened 2DMs-based devices for next-generation aerospace systems.

title: Modeling of the Test Mass Release Process Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm Identification and Adhesion Analysis
abstract: Gravitational waves carry a wealth of cosmic information, offering a new observation perspective for exploring the universe. The grabbing, positioning, and release mechanism is a fundamental element of the gravitational reference sensor used in spaceborne gravitational wave detectors and serves to steadily transition the test mass (TM) from high-load to geodetic conditions. However, implementing comprehensive performance testing on the entire mechanism will inevitably prolong the development period. Conversely, utilizing a dynamic model to predict the behavior of the released TM will facilitate the development and improvement of the mechanism. A dynamic model of the TM release process was established to assess the performance of the release mechanism and analyze the effect of adhesion on TM velocity. Firstly, a dynamic model of the release mechanism was developed, and the unknown parameters were identified using an identification method based on an improved genetic algorithm, which avoids the initial value of the parameters being challenging to guess. Then, considering the roughness of the contact surface between the release tip and the TM, the contact force was analyzed based on the Johnson–Kendall–Roberts theory. The dynamic model of the TM was formulated by incorporating the contact force into the release mechanism dynamic model, and the velocity response of the TM during unilateral release was calculated. Finally, the influence of mechanism parameters on the TM’s velocity was investigated. The TM velocity response indicates that adhesion does not considerably influence the TM velocity. Furthermore, the release mechanism can fulfill the mission requirements under typical release conditions.

title: Manure Amendments Improve Plant Growth and Productivity in Lunar Regolith Simulant
abstract: Plant cultivation on the Moon has garnered global scientific and engineering interest for its potential to support long-term human exploration and habitation. Lunar regolith, the natural medium for plant growth on the Moon, lacks organic matter and essential nutrients. This can pose challenges for lunar agriculture. Therefore, conditioning lunar regolith to enhance fertility and support plant growth is crucial. This study investigates the effects of animal manures as recycled organic waste on the growth and production of Brassica rapa , a commonly consumed vegetable, in a lunar simulant. The seeds of B. rapa were grown in the lunar regolith simulant amended with chicken and sheep manure at dosages of 0%, 5%, 10%, 25%, and 50% (w/w) for 20 days. At harvest, the sheep manure at 10% and 25% dosages significantly increased the shoot biomass of B. rapa (the edible part). The highest shoot production was observed in the 25% sheep manure treatment, resulting in a 98% increase in dry biomass compared to the control. This improvement was attributed to a significantly enhanced plant leaf area and thus increased light interception under sheep manure, particularly at 25% dosage. In contrast, chicken manure produced only a slight, statistically insignificant increase in biomass. This difference was attributed to the higher levels of plant-available P in a lunar simulant under sheep manure treatment, facilitating greater P uptake. Additionally, the increased enzyme activity in the sheep manure-treated lunar simulant enhanced carbon cycling, improving the fertility of the regolith for plant growth.

title: A Multidisciplinary Perspective on Interstellar, Interplanetary, and Intergalactic Travel: Technological, Legal, and Societal Implications
abstract: This paper presents a multidisciplinary exploration of the technological, legal, and societal implications of interstellar, interplanetary, and intergalactic travel. By integrating insights from space engineering, space law, and international relations, this paper examines the technological, legal, and societal implications of human expansion beyond Earth. It delves into critical questions such as the development of advanced propulsion systems, international cooperation, and ethical considerations, aiming to contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the future of human space exploration. Examining the intersection of space engineering and space law, this paper aims to identify the key challenges and opportunities associated with future human expansion into the cosmos. This paper argues that a paradigm shift is necessary to develop and implement innovative technologies, such as advanced propulsion systems, to enable interstellar and intergalactic travel. Additionally, this paper discusses the legal and ethical frameworks that will be required to govern human activities in space, ensuring the sustainable and equitable use of cosmic resources.

title: Observation Variable Framework for Exoplanet Habitability and Biosignatures
abstract: Since the first discovery of an exoplanet orbiting a Sun-like star in 1995, exoplanet research has shifted toward the exploration of habitable exoplanets and the identification of biosignatures within terrestrial-sized planets. As observation targets become more refined, there is a growing demand for more advanced observational capabilities, such as resolution, contrast, and sensitivity. Consequently, constructing an observation variable framework emerges as a cornerstone for addressing multifaceted mission tasks, including designing mission proposals, selecting observational targets, developing critical technologies, and analyzing observational data. In this context, we propose a methodology for the construction of an observation variable framework relating to habitability and biosignatures, founded on Bayesian theory. We elucidate the interrelationships between diverse elements and indicators across various hierarchical levels by integrating observational data, prior knowledge, and numerical models. This methodology enables a quantitative analysis of these indicators and serves as a reference for designing mission proposals, defining scientific targets, and researching on essential technologies.

title: Methods of Measuring Secondary Electron Yield for Space Dielectric Materials
abstract: The total secondary electron yield (SEY) of dielectric materials under pulse electron beam was investigated using the collector method. Accurate SEY characterization is essential for assessing surface charging effects in the space environment. However, SEY measurements of dielectrics, particularly easily charged Al 2 O 3 , are highly sensitive to both the performance of the measurement facilities and the surface conditions of materials. Two analytical models, dc output method and pulsed output method, were analyzed and compared. The results indicate that the single-pulsed method is more suitable for air-exposed metals and poorly conductive dielectrics, whereas for clean and contamination-free metals, the dc and pulsed yield models provide consistent SEY values. To obtain intrinsic, charging-free SEY data, measurements must be performed under low electron dose conditions with appropriate charge neutralization. Otherwise, the measured SEY exhibits an exponential decay under continuous electron pulses. In addition, excessive neutralization can also reduce the measured SEY below its intrinsic level. Based on the measurement methods, SEY values for several space dielectric materials were obtained. The results demonstrate that SEY is influenced by surface morphology, increasing with surface finishing from rough to ground or polished states. However, mechanical polishing shows little effect on SEY for smooth Al 2 O 3 surfaces with roughness below 0.30 μm. Among the investigated materials, polished Al 2 O 3 exhibits the highest SEY, with a maximum value of 7.72 ± 0.18 at an incident electron energy of 900 eV.

title: Satellite Formation Control for Cooperative Observation around the Rotating China Space Station
abstract: This study investigates the near-natural formation control of a nanosatellite cluster for cooperative observation of the China Space Station (CSS) with rotational motion. First, a CSS-centered inertial frame is introduced, and an open-loop dynamics model of the nanosatellite cluster is derived. Transformations of states, natural accelerations, and control accelerations among the CSS’s inertial, local-vertical local-horizontal (LVLH), and body frames are also established. Using a parametric 3-dimensional elliptic equation and analytical solutions for relative motion, the target formation configuration is defined and transformed into the CSS’s body frame, and can be designed to satisfy the collision avoidance constraints and the observation metric. A trajectory tracking control law is then designed in the body frame, demonstrating closed-loop Lyapunov stability. Finally, through simulations and performance analysis for both inertially orientated and transiently rotated attitudes of the CSS, it is verified that the proposed control law effectively guides the nanosatellite cluster to converge to the target formation and ensures obstacle avoidance, while the existing researches may fail to avoid the rotating complex-shaped obstacles and reach the target positions for lack of theoretical proofs. The control magnitudes are within acceptable limits, collision avoidance is ensured, and the observed mean full-coverage time closely matches the desired value.

title: Integrated Ground–Air–Space Exploration Technology of Jingpo Lake Lava Tubes
abstract: Lava tubes play an important role in base construction and understanding planetary geological development on extraterrestrial bodies. However, our understanding of lava tube morphology on Earth as a reference for extraterrestrial bodies remains limited. Existing research mainly focuses on their formation mechanisms and uses a single approach to study their morphology. To fill this gap, we conducted a multi-platform investigation of a lava tube near Jingpo Lake, Heilongjiang Province, China, employing space-, air-, and ground-based techniques. The method presented in this paper can assist in the comprehensive exploration of lunar lava tubes in the future. First, data covering this large lava tube area were collected using synthetic aperture radar (SAR), due to its all-weather capability, from which distribution information on lava tube skylights was retrieved. Furthermore, close-range point cloud data of the lava tube skylight areas were collected from drones equipped with the DJI Zenmuse L1 LiDAR sensor, which allows for high-resolution data acquisition and the creation of detailed models, providing local high-precision point clouds. Additionally, Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) was used for detailed point cloud collection inside the lava tubes, and through the registration of high-precision point clouds of the skylights both inside and outside the tube, comprehensive point cloud data of the entire lava tube were obtained. Hyperspectral LiDAR was also used to collect data of the tube walls under dark conditions, addressing the issue of consistency matching between hyperspectral imaging and laser far-field spots, enabling integrated spatial–spectral data acquisition. Finally, ground-penetrating radar was also employed for subsurface structural analysis, benefiting from its high penetration capabilities to acquire more detailed information on the underground morphology of the lava tubes. Our experiments demonstrate that this multi-sensor approach provides comprehensive information on terrain, lava tube orientation, cave distribution, and the internal environment of the lava tube system.

title: Sc-RNA seq Reveals the Protective Effects of Baoyuan Jieyu Formula on Spaceflight Depression Rats
abstract: Long-term spaceflight composite stress (LSCS) can induce detrimental impacts on the human central nervous system, leading to conditions such as depression. This study aimed to identify mechanisms of simulated LSCS-induced spaceflight depression and the protective effects of traditional Chinese medicine Baoyuan Jieyu Formula (BYJYF) on spaceflight depression rats. The present study simulated the real long-term space station environment by conducting a 6-week experiment that involved simulating microgravity, isolation, noise, circadian rhythm disruptions, and low pressure. Glutamatergic neuron firing in hippocampus of the rats was examined by patch clamp to explore the effects of simulated LSCS exposure and BYJYF intervention on neurons. Single-cell RNA sequencing was then conducted to reveal the underlying mechanisms of simulated LSCS-induced spaceflight depression and the efficiency of BYJYF intervention. Results showed that simulated LSCS caused glutamate overload, induced by an abnormally high release frequency ( P < 0.05) from glutamatergic neurons. Single-cell sequencing revealed that the possible causes of glutamate overload lied in the reduction in hippocampal stromal cells, especially astrocytes, thereby delaying glutamate clearance, which could be mitigated by BYJYF intervention by up-regulating the proportion of stromal cells. Transcriptomics revealed that the target pathway of simulated LSCS-induced spaceflight depression was the calcium signaling pathway, and BYJYF functioned by regulating genes related to long-term potentiation pathway. Taken together, we demonstrate the target pathways of simulated LSCS-induced spaceflight depression and the potential clinical application of BYJYF, opening up broader prospects for the application of traditional Chinese medicine in space medicine.

title: Enabling Internet Surfing for Civil Aviation: The Last Piece of the Coverage Puzzle
abstract: Because of the ever-increasing goal of obtaining global coverage and upgrading terrestrial communication systems, delivering universal and cost-effective data services in civil aircraft has become crucial. This is seen as an important piece in establishing seamless data coverage globally and has gained considerable attention. In this article, our objective is to propose communication frameworks that will offer high-quality internet service to aircraft passengers. The development of satellites and high-altitude platforms could be implemented to provide data coverage on civil aircraft. Terrestrial networks, e.g., developing the sixth generation of wireless communication techniques, can also play a vital role in such communication systems. In this article, we first investigate the properties of civil aircraft airlines before proposing communication frameworks for different categories of civil aircraft communications. The performance of energy consumption, latency, and outage probability is then evaluated to demonstrate these methods’ pros and cons. Finally, the key challenges and research directions for the future have been discussed and analyzed.

title: An Economic Framework for Space Immigration
abstract: Large-scale, voluntary space settlement must be economically rational to be viable. Here, we deploy the Roy model, an economic model used to understand immigration, to illuminate the economic factors important for space settlement and develop qualitative understanding of robust features of space settlement that do not depend on the details of the space economy. We find that getting the cost of living in space down by approximately 2 orders of magnitude is necessary to generate a space population on the order of 1 million people and the typical net utility of immigrating will be on the order of this cost. In addition, if the space economy is driven by productive activities of space settlers and there is some correlation between Earth and space skills and income, space settlers are likely to be drawn from the upper tail of Earth income distribution. An ideal way to incentivize immigration by these high-skill, high-income individuals is to declare the space economy free of redistributive taxes. Alternatively, if space settlement is driven by an insurance policy on civilization involving monetary transfers from Earth to space settlers, the space settlers are likely to be drawn from the lower tail of Earth income distribution, and only minimal marginal income beyond the cost of living in space will be necessary to create positive net utility of immigrating for them. The usefulness of the Roy model is demonstrated by its flexibility in providing qualitative insight in these disparate situations.

title: Adaptive Near-Propellant-Optimal Powered Descent Initiation for Human Mars Landing
abstract: Future human Mars missions will typically require pinpoint landing, defined as achieving a touchdown error within 100 m. To ensure mission success, the powered descent phase should be initiated under favorable conditions. This paper proposes an adaptive powered descent initiation (PDI) strategy based on a constant-thrust-magnitude propellant-optimal guidance algorithm. The adaptive PDI strategy selects the initiation condition by maximizing the safety circle radius. Key supporting technologies include a rapid solution method for the optimal control problem, which leverages closed-form vehicle state expressions and dimensionality reduction of the underlying system of equations, as well as an efficient landing footprint prediction algorithm based on uniform angular interval directional search. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed methods are computationally efficient and reliably establish favorable initiation conditions, making subsequent pinpoint landing not only feasible but also robust against trajectory dispersion.

title: Modeling of Forward/Inverse Kinematics and Closed-Loop Control for Soft Robotic Arms
abstract: Soft robotic arms offer a novel and secure technical approach for assisting astronauts in space stations, owing to their unique advantages such as flexibility and safety in human–machine interaction. During astronaut operational assistance, the forward and inverse kinematics models serve as the theoretical foundation for achieving interactive control. Typically, forward kinematics calculates the end position based on control inputs, while inverse kinematics determines the necessary inputs to achieve a desired position. Existing methods encounter challenges due to the large deformations and redundancies of the arms, which can lead to numerical instability or high data requirements. This study presents an innovative kinematic approach specifically designed for pneumatic soft arms. The forward model employs a fitting function, while the inverse kinematics is formulated as a constrained optimization problem that minimizes the deviation of the end position from the target. Experiments demonstrate that the forward fitting method is effective for both single and multichamber actuators. The inverse optimization substantially enhances control robustness and ensures motion convergence. This algorithm serves as a foundation for closed-loop feedback control, facilitating precise positioning. Demonstrations indicate that the proposed method enables rapid positioning through a single optimization calculation and achieves precise positioning with closed-loop control based on the optimization, offering promising extensions to other types of pneumatic robotic arms. The forward and inverse kinematics algorithm proposed in this paper provides a theoretical basis for the application of soft robotic arms in space operation assistive missions.

title: A Novel RGB-D Camera Based Dataset for Spacecraft Pose Estimation
abstract: In the field of close-proximity space operations, RGB-D cameras have been used widely. However, publicly available spacecraft datasets for pose estimation are primarily based solely on image data. There is no publicly available dataset based on RGB-D cameras that can be directly used. Therefore, this paper introduces a novel RGB-D camera based spacecraft (RDCS) dataset. Due to high acquisition costs and confidentiality issues, it is difficult to obtain real spacecraft data and their associated pose information. To address this, the space environment and camera trajectories are constructed in Blender to capture pixel-aligned RGB images and depth maps of spacecraft from various observation angles. In addition, the RDCS dataset also includes pose annotations, bounding box labels, and corresponding mask images. The process focuses on addressing the challenges of acquiring the RGB image and the depth map of the spacecraft at the same keyframe while ensuring their pixel alignment, as well as determining the corresponding pose annotations. Finally, a spacecraft pose estimation network based on the pixel-level fused feature is applied to verify the availability of the RDCS dataset.

title: Enhancing the Stability of LISA-Like Formations via Scale-Factor Adjustment and Energy Matching
Frequency-Sweeping Interferometry for Intersatellite Baseline Metrology in Array Telescope Formation
abstract: Space-based distributed array telescope formations hold substantial potential for deep space exploration, with their performance highly dependent on precise baseline measurements between subtelescopes. This study presents a double-sideband frequency-sweeping interferometry (DSB-FSI) technique based on electro-optic modulation for intertelescope baseline measurements. To address the lack of on-orbit frequency-sweep calibration references, a Fabry–Pérot etalon is used for real-time in situ frequency-sweep rate calibration. Experimental results show that the Fabry–Pérot etalon effectively calibrates the frequency-sweep rate of the DSB-FSI system, reducing long-term baseline measurement drift error from 20.11 to 13.38 μm and decreasing maximum measurement deviation from 18.03 to 13.14 μm over a 5.7-m baseline. Metrological calibration confirms that the calibrated system achieves a baseline measurement accuracy of 44.30 μm over a 10-m range, with excellent dynamic measurement performance for monitoring baseline variations. The DSB-FSI technique is expected to provide a reliable solution for the high-precision intertelescope baseline measurements in “MEAYIN” (Multiple-Spacecraft Exoplanet Aperture Synthetic Interferometer) project, thus supporting the advancement of space-based distributed array telescope formation technologies.

title: Analysis of Defense Technology for Large-Sized Near-Earth Asteroids
abstract: Mitigating the risk of near-Earth asteroid (NEA) impacts is critical to global security and the survival of human civilization. In particular, large NEAs with short warning times pose a devastating threat to humanity. The most effective defense method is to directly destroy or rapidly deflect its orbit using the enormous energy generated by detonation, and, in extreme cases, it is the only feasible method. Based on a comparative analysis of different detonation defense types, this paper investigates detonation defense modes for large NEAs. Two defense modes are proposed, including a novel flyby preexcavation detonation defense mode. A comparative analysis of influencing factors and effectiveness is conducted for both modes, revealing their respective effects on large NEAs. The 2 defense modes exhibit distinct characteristics. For large NEAs with limited warning times, the proposed novel detonation defense mode is found to have lower technical complexity and better defense efficacy, making it a preferred method. This study can provide references for the engineering design of defense against large NEAs.

title: Mission Planning for Very-Low-Earth-Orbit Technology Exploration of ELITE with Collision Avoidance Ability
abstract: Everything else being equal, operating at a very low Earth orbit (VLEO) gives better ground resolution compared to operating at higher altitudes. However, operating at a VLEO faces marked atmospheric drag and various other uncertain interference factors. In this paper, we describe a pioneering satellite named ELITE (Extremely Low-earth Imaging and Technology Explorer) for high-resolution imaging and solar activity observation in VLEO. ELITE is planned to launch to an altitude of 550 km (Sun-synchronous orbit), then maneuver to a VLEO within the range of 200 to 350 km, and maintain that altitude for a year in VLEO through electrical propulsion. To address the challenges of VLEOs, a multiphase altitude planning framework is proposed, covering 4 critical scenarios that account for atmospheric drag, solar activity forecasts, and the strict requirements of time delay integration imaging. This enables robust and energy-efficient altitude adjustment strategies for stable long-term operation. An atmospheric density model is also developed, integrating solar activity predictions, drag coefficient estimation, public datasets, and onboard measurements, and validated using real VLEO mission data. A risk-aware collision avoidance strategy based on a beta-distributed differential evolution algorithm is introduced to balance safety and fuel efficiency, ensuring fast convergence during different evolutionary stages. These innovations ensure that ELITE can successfully accomplish its VLEO mission objectives: a groundbreaking 0.5-m ground sampling distance in color and innovative measurements of ionospheric intensity and atomic oxygen in VLEO. Our mission planning confirms ELITE’s capability to accomplish its missions, marking an important milestone in the field of VLEO satellites.

title: Physical Modeling of Degradation Failure Mechanism of Rhenium–Tungsten Filaments in Mass Spectrometers of Environmental Control and Life Support System: Electromigration, Thermal Effect, and Coupled Oxidation
abstract: In aerospace missions, the proper functioning of the environmental control and life support system (ECLSS) is critical to ensuring mission success. As a key gas detection device in the ECLSS, the performance of the rhenium–tungsten (Re–W) filament in the ion source of quadrupole mass spectrometers directly affects the stability and data accuracy of the instrument. However, tungsten alloy filaments may still suffer damage due to thermal stress, electromigration, mild oxidation, and other factors during operation. Therefore, investigating the damage mechanisms of Re–W filaments is of substantial practical importance. This study aims to explore the failure mechanisms of Re–W filaments and provide a basis for performance improvement in practical applications. The paper systematically introduces the working principle of quadrupole mass spectrometers, details the construction of the experimental platform, and conducts filament failure experiments under high-temperature electrified conditions in a vacuum environment. Subsequently, scanning electron microscopy and x-ray diffraction were employed to analyze both intact and damaged Re–W filaments, elucidating their failure mechanisms. Experimental results reveal the potential causes of filament damage during failure processes, including electromigration, thermal-stress-induced damage, and oxidation. This study represents the first systematic investigation into the failure mechanisms of Re–W filaments in quadrupole mass spectrometers, offering experimental evidence and technical support for future performance enhancement strategies. These findings contribute to improving the reliability of ECLSSs and the success rate of aerospace missions.

title: Interference Coupling Characteristics and Suppression of High-Power EMP for Satellite Power Systems
abstract: The transient intense high-power electromagnetic pulse radiation in space can have a serious impact on the normal operation of in-orbit satellites. Especially for satellite electrical power systems (EPSs), electromagnetic pulses will be coupled to the power condition unit inside the satellite cabin through external solar arrays, leading to serious electromagnetic interference (EMI) problems in the satellite EPSs. In order to analyze the coupling degree of electromagnetic pulse interference on satellite power systems, an EMI experiment system for satellite EPSs was established and interference voltage levels both on the input and output ports of the power controller under severe electromagnetic pulse interference were obtained. The overvoltage of the output bus can reach 500 V, and the interference frequency exceeds 10 MHz, and the coupling characteristics of EMI have been verified through a simulation analysis system. Furthermore, an electromagnetic pulse interference suppression technique based on an isolation transformer with deep EMI suppression together with a novel discrete winding transformer LLC resonant converter was proposed to address the EMI coupling characteristics of satellite EPSs. An electromagnetic pulse interference suppression performance experiment was conducted on the core component of this suppression measure, namely, the novel deep suppression isolation transformer, and it was proved that with the anti-electromagnetic pulse method, the EMI level of the satellite power system could be suppressed effectively, and the shielding effectiveness of electromagnetic pulse was up to 56 dB.

title: Prospect and Research Progress of Lunar Intelligent Robot Technology
abstract: The field of aerospace technology is currently undergoing rapid development, with the focus of human space endeavors shifting from near-Earth space to lunar space. The establishment of lunar research stations and lunar bases, which represent large-scale deep space exploration, is gradually becoming a reality. These increasingly complex lunar exploration scenarios give rise to novel demands for the development of lunar intelligent robot technology. The rapid development of artificial intelligence and robotic technology in recent years, coupled with the application of deep learning, large models, and embodied intelligence, has resulted in the emergence of intelligent robots. A comprehensive examination of the integration of deep space exploration and robotic technology is imperative. Firstly, the demand for lunar surface operational capabilities is examined within the context of advancing human lunar exploration. A developmental roadmap for lunar robots is proposed, along with categorization methods. Secondly, the main technical challenges encountered in complex professional scenarios on the lunar surface are outlined. Additionally, design concepts, technical approaches, and key technology systems for lunar intelligent robots are presented. Finally, targeted experimental validation is provided for the key technologies.

title: Attention-Mechanism-Based Method for Many-to-Many Orbital Reconnaissance with Limited Payloads
abstract: The many-to-many orbital reconnaissance (MMOR) scheduling problem focuses on optimizing the sequences of target inspections performed by reconnaissance satellites to minimize the costs of orbit transfers. As satellite constellations continue to expand, the complexity of planning MMOR missions has increased significantly, rendering traditional optimization methods inadequate for meeting real-time requirements. To tackle these challenges, we propose an innovative attention-based learning method aimed at enhancing the decision-making capabilities of reconnaissance satellites. We begin by formulating the MMOR problem in the form of a capacitated vehicle routing problem, a formulation that simplifies the problem by normalizing the payload capacities of reconnaissance satellites and the resource demands of the targets. We then design a neural network with an attention mechanism, which is trained using the REINFORCE algorithm. This model allows satellites to dynamically determine the inspection sequences. Through extensive simulations, we evaluate the impact of different hyperparameters and identify optimal configurations that maximize performance. Our results demonstrate that the proposed model consistently achieves near-optimal performance compared to traditional metaheuristic methods. Moreover, it exhibits strong generalization capabilities, performing exceptionally well across various scenarios with different target quantities. These findings suggest that the method could be useful for improving the efficiency of satellite mission planning.

title: Low-Thrust Earth–Moon Trajectory Design Using Successive Convex Programming
abstract: The Earth–Moon cargo spacecraft is essential for the sustainable development and utilization of lunar resources. The application of a high-specific-impulse, low-thrust propulsion system can substantially improve payload efficiency. However, the perturbed dynamics of the Earth–Moon 3-body system pose marked convergence challenges in low-thrust trajectory optimization. This paper proposes an enhanced sequential convex programming (SCP) method for optimizing low-thrust transfer trajectories between the primary and secondary bodies in arbitrary 3-body systems, which is also applicable to the Earth–Moon scenario. The proposed approach enhances algorithmic convergence by introducing an improved initial profile. First, an approach for constructing the initial profile is presented, in which the primary-body to secondary-body trajectory is divided into 2 phases: escape from one body and capture by the other body. Initial trajectories are designed using the indirect method under the 2-body model for each phase, and the 2 segments are concatenated to form the improved profile. Next, the SCP approach utilizing the enhanced profile is presented, replacing the traditional linear interpolation profile with the more feasible improved profile, thereby enhancing the algorithm’s convergence. Finally, the method is applied to design fuel-optimal transfer trajectories from either highly elliptical Earth orbits or inclined geosynchronous orbits to the lunar polar orbit. The results show that when the SCP algorithm based on a linear interpolation profile fails to identify a feasible solution, the proposed method successfully achieves convergence to one. By applying thrust-magnitude homotopy, the method transitions the fuel-optimal solution toward a near-time-optimal one. The proposed method offers substantial potential for trajectory design in future transportation missions between 2 celestial bodies, particularly for the Earth–Moon scenario.

title: Manufacturing and Joining of Composite Units for On-Orbit Construction of Large Structures in Space
abstract: On-orbit construction eliminates the need to withstand the harsh mechanical environment during the launch phase and is not constrained by the size limitations of a launch vehicle’s fairing. This approach effectively reduces the structural weight of spacecraft and enables the construction of space facilities on scales ranging from hundreds to even thousands of kilometers. Truss-type structures are the primary support structures for large-scale space bodies. Therefore, the 2 key technologies in on-orbit construction are the fabrication of large structural units and the connection between these units. This paper proposes the use of carbon fiber/polyetheretherketone (CF/PEEK) composite prepreg tapes to manufacture composite tubular units through the pultrusion process. The influence of temperature and speed on the mechanical properties of the pultruded tubular units was studied. Additionally, it proposes using 3-dimensionally printed translucent PEEK joints to connect the tubular units, reinforced by laser transmission welding. The effects of welding temperature and speed on the weld strength were analyzed, and the microstructural characteristics of the weld were observed at a microscopic scale. Finally, a parabolic antenna framework was fabricated by cutting CF/PEEK composite tubular units into different lengths, verifying the feasibility of this method for on-orbit construction. This paper offers a valuable technical reference for the advancement of on-orbit construction technology.

title: Unsupervised Change Detection for Auroral Activity in Ground-based All-Sky Imager Observation
abstract: Aurora phenomenon is the most visible manifestation of space weather and play a crucial role in geoscientific studies of near-Earth space processes. Segmenting auroral image sequences from large vast observational data is vital for statistical study and determining the lifetime of auroral events. In particular, discovering auroral motion features from big data requires automatic classification and retrieval of auroral motion patterns. Using individual images or randomly segmented fixed-length subsequences as training samples is not appropriate. For untrimmed auroral videos of any length, this paper proposes an unsupervised framework to break down long sequences into shorter temporal units without predefined classes. Sparse and low-rank decomposition theory is used to process auroral morphological and motion information at both pixel level and sequence level, which ensures that both macroscopic variations in auroral sequences and local key structures in auroral images can be taken into account in calculating the difference between consecutive sequences. Experiments conducted on all-sky image sequences obtained at Yellow River Station show that our method achieves high performance for auroral activity change detection. The proposed approach provides an effective tool for monitoring auroral activities and parsing a continuous stream of auroral activity into meaningful events, which enables the statistical study of auroral behavior based on big data.

title: Active Defense Guidance for Spacecraft in Multi-Strategy Engagement with Incomplete Information
abstract: This paper investigates the active defense guidance problem for spacecraft in a multi-strategy target–pursuer–defender scenario, where a target spacecraft with an active defender attempts to evade the pursuer. Considering the practical applications, the pursuer may adopt variable possible interception strategies, and it brings the multi-strategy engagement problem for the target spacecraft. The active defense guidance not only contends with such engagement uncertainties but also needs to handle the incomplete information and observation noise during the whole process. By modeling the scenario as a multiple partially observable Markov decision process, this paper proposes a spacecraft active defense guidance based on an adaptive dueling double deep Q-network (AD 3 QN) reinforcement learning algorithm. To effectively address the partial observation problem caused by multi-strategy engagement, the AD 3 QN algorithm utilizes a fusion structure of convolutional and recurrent networks that enables the extraction of fragmented information characteristics and time-dependent data modeling. Moreover, a mechanism, which can stack the input observations and reshape the buffer arrangement, is designed to process the incomplete information. Based on this, the networks extract state features and trajectory characteristic tensors from the stacked time series observations, enhancing the agent’s estimation and identification abilities. With the proposed AD 3 QN-based guidance method, the target spacecraft exhibits robust performance even in the presence of incomplete information and multi-strategy engagement. Finally, the performance of the AD 3 QN-based policy is evaluated through numerical experiments.

title: Optimal Transfers from the L1 Halo Orbit of the Earth–Moon System to Earth
abstract: Designing direct-return orbits from the Earth–Moon space to Earth’s surface is critical for manned lunar missions and emergency returns. This paper investigates optimal transfer solutions from a halo orbit around the Earth–Moon L1 libration point to an Earth reentry point. Cislunar L1 orbits are commonly utilized as habitats for spacecraft involved in various missions, necessitating the development of a minimum-fuel transfer strategy between L1 orbits and Earth for future complex applications within the Earth–Moon system. We suggest a novel design method that leverages the accessibility of halo orbit pseudomanifolds to closer Earth orbits, enabling efficient transfers through a single impulsive maneuver along the unstable pseudomanifold trajectory. To overcome the challenge of local optima resulting from numerous optimization variables, we employ an enhanced particle swarm optimization with gray wolf optimizer algorithm. This method aims to minimize the Δ V transfer costs within the circular restricted 3-body problem framework. Our results demonstrate low and feasible flight times and are expected to provide valuable reference for the design and implementation of future Earth–Moon transfer orbits.

title: Robust Leader-Following Consensus Control of Multiple Nonholonomic Lunar Wheeled Robot Systems with Disturbances and Time-Varying Input Delays
abstract: To tackle the leader-following consensus tracking problem in multiple nonholonomic lunar wheeled robot systems under disturbances and time-varying input delays, a robust control strategy composed of 3 key components is developed in this paper. First, distributed state and input observers are designed to obtain the leader’s state/input information, while extended state observers are used to estimate the disturbances. Then, a compound consensus controller is developed by integrating a nonlinear delay compensator with the backstepping control technique to handle unknown disturbances and attenuate the adverse effects of input delays. Furthermore, the leader-following consensus analysis via Lyapunov–Krasovskii stability theory is conducted. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is validated through numerical simulations involving a group of lunar wheeled robots subject to longitudinal slip disturbances and time-varying input delays.

title: Optimization of Geocentric Gravitational-Wave Observatory Using High-Order State Transition Tensor
Delayed Detached Eddy Simulation of a Transverse Supersonic Jet into Hypersonic Crossflow
abstract: In both military and civil industries, the complex flow field induced by a jet exhausting has widespread applications, such as supersonic/hypersonic vehicle reaction control systems, thrust vector control systems on rocket motors, and supersonic combustion. The jet interaction flow field involves complex unsteady shocks, spatial vortex, and separated flow and shear layer; the traditional Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes equations failed to predict these unsteady characteristics and perform poor in separated flow. In this study, the supersonic jet exhausting into a hypersonic crossflow is investigated by the delayed detached eddy simulation (DDES). The typical mean flow properties and the instantaneous flow properties are analyzed. Results show that calculated data agreed well with the experimental data. DDES is also capable of resolving and capturing the detailed flow structures.

title: Research on thermal characteristics of a reusable vehicle during re-entry into the atmosphere
Pre-rerouting Strategy to Ensure Business Continuity for Low-Earth-Orbit Satellite Network
abstract: In a satellite network, due to the relative movement between satellites in different orbits or different layers, the intersatellite link changes dynamically. These changes are further classified into 2 main groups: some of them are predictable, such as link interruptions caused by changes in the relative positions of satellites in different orbits or different layers, while others are unpredictable, such as link interruptions caused by cosmic rays in the free-space environment, effects of the solar wind, or damages to satellite equipment. Such intersatellite link interruptions will cause severe service interruptions. For predictable link interruptions, this study proposes a pre-rerouting strategy based on the extended Open Shortest Path First protocol where a new label switching path (LSP) is built and services are switched to the new LSP before the old LSP is interrupted. In this case, the packet loss rate will be substantially reduced, ensuring a high degree of service continuity. In a performance verification experiment, simulation results show that the packet loss rate decreased by about 6% compared with that of the traditional rerouting strategy.

title: Hierarchical Motion Planning Method for Space Redundant Manipulators with End-Task Constraint
abstract: This paper proposes a hierarchical motion planning method integrating goal-biased rapidly exploring random tree (GB-RRT) and sequential convex programming (SCP) for a class of space redundant manipulators (SRM) utilizing an end hand–eye camera to perform visual monitoring tasks. By analyzing the main influencing factors in an SRM system, the nonlinear optimal control problem model that incorporates kinematics, dynamics, obstacle avoidance, and line-of-sight constraints is first developed to describe the trajectory planning of SRM. Next, to warm-start the solution of the SCP program, a trajectory planning algorithm based on GB-RRT and cubic spline curves is designed at the kinematics level to rapidly plan collision-free and smooth reference trajectories. Then, all the constraints at the dynamics level are convexified with the help of the velocity damping method, quaternion differentiation, first-order Taylor expansion, and continuous linearization techniques. As a result, the optimal solution of the original planning problem can be obtained by solving the new SCP problem, in which the accuracy of the solution is guaranteed by applying trust region constraints to the key variables. The proposed hierarchical planning method not only avoids the poor scalability issue of the sampling-based motion planning method when considering complex constraints, but also provides high-quality initial reference trajectories for solving the SCP program. Finally, some numerical simulations are provided to verify the effectiveness and validity of the proposed method.

title: Gaussian Smoothing Technique for Eclipse-Constrained Cislunar Multi-Mode Trajectory Optimization
abstract: The presence of discontinuous path constraints and optimal bang-bang control profiles in indirect trajectory optimization may lead to integral discontinuities and exacerbate the sensitivity problem of the initial costate. In this manuscript, we incorporate a multimode electric propulsion system into a low-thrust trajectory optimization problem subject to shadow constraints in cislunar space. The forced engine shutdown in shadowing and the rapid switching between different propulsion modes exacerbate the nonlinearity of the optimization problem. An indirect optimal control formulation for the multimode propulsion system is derived, and a control smoothing method based on the Gaussian error function is proposed. The 13-type minimum-fuel transfer problem between 4 cislunar periodic orbits under all possible shadowing conditions is resolved through the utilization of a set of parameterized S-shaped curves, which gradually approximate the discontinuity profiles. A comparative analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the technique, and the distribution of the arc segments and the embedding pattern of the shadow arcs were discussed.

title: A Porous Bioelastomer with Negative Poisson’s Ratio: Toward Eco-friendly and Flexible Applications
abstract: As an emerging soft functional material, poly(glycerol sebacate) (PGS) has found substantial applications across a broad spectrum of engineering practices. This study reports the preparation of porous PGS materials with negative Poisson’s ratios through polycondensation and the salt-leaching method. The microscopic pore structures and dynamic mechanical properties of these PGS materials with negative Poisson’s ratios are quantitatively characterized by using scanning electron microscopy and a dynamic mechanical analyzer. These quantitative characterizations will provide technical support and innovative perspectives for the design of novel materials in aerospace engineering, as well as for the development of eco-friendly and flexible applications.

title: Spacecraft System-Level Survivability Assessment Method Considering Secondary Debris Cloud Damage
abstract: Space debris and micrometeoroids have become one of the sources of risk for the safe operation of spacecraft in orbit. Damage caused by impacts at different velocities is inconsistent. Particles fragment upon non-low-velocity impact, forming a debris cloud that can damage internal components. This paper establishes a hypervelocity impact vulnerability assessment model of internal spacecraft components based on the debris cloud model (DCM). By integrating the DCM and ray-tracing method, the deficiency of the ballistic limit equation method in describing the damage effects of secondary debris on internal components is addressed. This integrative model ensures more accurate computations and achieves a more realistic simulation of internal component vulnerabilities during the hypervelocity impact vulnerability assessment process. Building on this model, a spacecraft system-level survivability assessment method based on dynamic Bayesian networks is proposed, taking into account the possibility of common cause failures (CCFs) induced by secondary debris clouds. This approach removes the assumption that component failures are independent, which is inherent in previous non-CCF models. The results indicate that the use of a non-CCF model can adversely affect the survivability assessment of the system, leading to suboptimal redundancy design.

title: A Predictive Learning-Based Pursuit Strategy for the Multiple-to-One Orbital Pursuit–Evasion Game
abstract: The scarcity of space orbit resources has intensified the issue of orbital games between spacecraft. This paper presents a control strategy for the pursuing spacecraft in a multiple-to-one orbital pursuit–evasion game problem. Initially, a mathematical model is established for the multiple-to-one orbital pursuit–evasion game problem, incorporating impulse maneuvers for both the pursuing and evasive spacecraft. This model also considers the maximum single velocity increment and maximum total velocity increment restrictions imposed on the spacecraft. Subsequently, a method for constructing a pursuing policy, which integrates evasive spacecraft action prediction and the deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm, is proposed. The pursuing policy network and the evasive spacecraft action prediction network are trained under a centralized training and decentralized execution framework. The evasive spacecraft action prediction network can predict the actions of the evasive spacecraft based on the states observed by the pursuing spacecraft. It then predicts the subsequent state of the evasive spacecraft through the control model, providing supplementary information for the decision-making process of the pursuing policy. The simulation results indicate that the pursuing policy, enhanced by the prediction of the evasive spacecraft’s actions, outperforms the traditional deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm in both the training stage and statistical performance. Furthermore, the prediction of the evasive spacecraft’s actions can compensate for the numerical and maneuverability deficiencies of the pursuing spacecraft. However, a key limitation of this approach is its reliance on prior action data of the evasive spacecraft.

title: Monitoring Cognitive Brain Function Before and After Spaceflight: Feasibility of Brain Vital Signs
abstract: Space exploration provides a unique opportunity to study human physiology under extreme conditions, such as microgravity and radiation exposure. A thorough understanding of both cognitive performance and neurophysiological adaptations in this extreme condition is missing in previous literature. This study is a methodological demonstration of comparing cognitive performance and electroencephalography (EEG) brain vital signs in 2 astronauts before, shortly after, and 5 months following a 17-d mission to the International Space Station. Cognitive task performance remained consistent between pre- and post-spaceflight measures. Similarly, EEG brain vital signs revealed minimal change in the time-frequency domain. These findings suggest that short-duration spaceflight, combined with sufficient Earth adaptation time, showed no major decrements in cognitive and neurophysiological function. This study underscores for the first time the feasibility for EEG brain vital sign approaches to monitor brain health and investigate brain function at an individual level, which is critical during space missions.

title: Asteroid 2024 YR4: A Comprehensive Impact Risk Analysis with the SHARP-TWS System
Review of the Development of Energy Technology Experiment for Space Station
abstract: Space energy technology constitutes a comprehensive technological system designed to meet the energy acquisition, storage, conversion, management, and transmission requirements for spacecraft’s long-term operation in space environments, serving as a critical core technology for maintaining sustained and stable operation of various spacecraft and manned space stations. Space stations, characterized by long-term microgravity, large-scale vacuum, temperature cycling, and radiation environments, provide exceptional verification conditions for testing new space technologies. Given the paramount importance of space energy technology in space applications, nations worldwide have conducted extensive experiments aboard space stations, encompassing various forms of solar cell technologies, space battery systems, energy conversion technologies, and power transmission methods, thereby accumulating substantial technical reserves for innovative development in this field. The space-based energy technology system is comprehensively discussed in this paper through 4 key aspects: energy generation technologies, energy storage technologies, energy conversion technologies, and energy transmission technologies. A systematic analysis is conducted on energy technology experimental research performed aboard both domestic and international space stations. Representative on-orbit verification experiments and their achievements are summarized, while the developmental characteristics of scientific experimental support technologies across different space station programs are comparatively analyzed. The technological outcomes derived from space station energy experiments and their promoting effects on technical advancement are thoroughly reviewed. Finally, recommendations for future space station energy technology experiments are proposed.

title: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Satellite Evasion Tasks in Limited Observable and Orbit-Constrained Environments
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) holds promise for the automated control of satellite orbits and the avoidance of spatial obstacles due to its ability to learn and adapt to dynamic environments through interaction, enabling autonomous, real-time decision-making for orbit adjustments. Satellite orbit control tasks manifest strong nonlinear characteristics, for which algorithms grounded on neural networks are more adept at handling. However, RL methods based on neural networks, which are highly nonconvex and nonsmooth functions, sometimes yield extreme action values that are not conducive to the orbit-constrained task at hand. In addition, in practical satellite task environments, limited observability is often faced. This limited observability not only increases the complexity of the algorithm but also affects the efficiency of identifying appropriate actions. To address this issue, we introduce a hierarchical parameterization mechanism to accelerate the search for appropriate actions. Hence, we introduce the integration of self-attention mechanisms with the Kalman filter into RL frameworks to accommodate scenarios with limited observability. Experimental results demonstrate a marked increase in the success rate of automated evasion maneuvers in environments with limited observability and orbital constraints, when facing pursuing satellites. Then, we performed a comparative analysis, applying Lambert guidance and RL-based guidance as control strategies for powerful confinement environment to validate our algorithm’s robustness.

title: SCABS for In-situ Volatile Quantitative Analysis of Lunar Regolith: Design and Validation
The Orbital Evolution of 2 Binary Asteroid Systems Based on Hamel’s Variational Integrators
abstract: In the full n -body problem, the mutual gravitational potential energy of the rigid body is determined by its position and attitude, which leads to the coupling of the translational and rotational motions. This paper focuses on the comprehensive full 2-body problem comprising 2 double asteroids. Because of the small distance and the relatively small mass difference between the 2 asteroids, it is assumed that the distance remains constant during the modeling process. In other words, each binary system is treated as a rigid “dumbbell” system. In this paper, special Euclidean group SE 3 is used to describe the configuration of the dumbbell-shaped body, and both the continuous equations of motion based on Hamilton’s principle and discrete ones based on discrete Hamilton’s principle are derived. The discrete equations of motion, known as Hamel’s variational integrators, are accurate and efficient for simulating the full 2-body dynamics of double dumbbells. Hamel’s variational integrators can preserve symplectic structure, system momentum, Lie group structure, and conserve energy over an extended time span. The simulation results indicate that Hamel’s variational integrators exhibit improved accuracy and superior preservation of geometric structures compared to Runge–Kutta methods and Lie group variational integrators.

title: NADPH Oxidase/Antioxidant Dual-Target Intervention Reduces Radiation-Induced Embryo Defects in Mice
abstract: The potential adverse effects of chronic exposure to extremely low doses of ionizing radiation on early mammalian embryonic development, particularly during the preimplantation stage, remains a topic of ongoing debate due to the lack of definitive evidence. Here, we investigate the effects of spaceflight-associated low-dose radiation on early mammalian development in mice. Using in vitro cultured one-cell embryos exposed to varying cumulative low doses of Cs-137 rays, we demonstrate that 2 mGy of radiation markedly impairs blastocyst development. Transcriptomic profiling reveals altered gene expression associated with oxidative stress, organogenesis, and developmental processes. Furthermore, in vivo exposure of pregnant mice to 10 mGy radiation results in reduced litter size, birth weight, and crown–rump length, with these effects emerging during implantation and fetal growth. Notably, pre- and during-radiation supplementation with NADPH oxidase inhibitor apocynin and vitamin C mitigates developmental defects, including the reversal of radiation-induced gene expression and histone modification changes. These findings demonstrate that chronic low-dose ionizing radiation disrupts both pre- and postimplantation embryo development in a dose-dependent manner, while highlighting the potential of antioxidant interventions to counteract radiation-induced developmental damage.

title: Carbon-Based High-Thermal-Conductivity Materials for Thermal Management in Space Optical Sensors
abstract: Effective thermal management is essential for aerospace applications, particularly for space optical remote sensors (SORSs) that rely on advanced materials for efficient heat dissipation and storage. Carbon-based materials have emerged as prominent solutions due to their superior thermal conductivity, lightweight nature, and mechanical strength. This review highlights the crucial role of carbon-based materials in SORS thermal management, offering an overview of their properties and applications. It also explores the challenges faced in implementing these materials and outlines future research directions. By connecting current knowledge with recent advancements, this review aims to emphasize the transformative potential of carbon-based materials in the thermal management of SORSs, highlighting both their current impact and future prospects.

title: Research on an Attitude Controllable Radar Image Generation Method for Noncooperative Targets
abstract: The generation of radar images of noncooperative targets has always been a hot topic and difficulty in this field. Although the existing methods based on generative adversarial networks can solve the problem of insufficient number of radar images of noncooperative targets, they lack precise control over the target’s pose during image generation. In view of this, inspired by the ControlNet model’s ability to incorporate additional conditions for controllable generation in optical image synthesis, this paper develops a method for generating radar images of noncooperative targets with precise pose control based on the ControlNet model. In this paper, the geometric model of noncooperative targets is first constructed, and a limited number of target radar images are obtained through electromagnetic calculation. Secondly, a frequency domain denoising method is proposed to filter out the stripe noise in the radar images; meanwhile, Lee filter is applied to remove speckle noise from the radar images, thus building a database of radar images for noncooperative targets. Finally, the edge map of the optical images under different poses are used as control conditions to realize the generation of radar images of noncooperative targets with precise and controllable poses based on the ControlNet model. Simulation results demonstrate that this method can generate radar images of noncooperative targets with accurately controlled azimuth and elevation angles. Especially when the number of training samples is limited, the generated results outperform existing algorithms in terms of structural similarity, peak signal-to-noise ratio, and Fréchet inception distance.

title: Task manifold-based control scheme for a micro co-axial dual-rotor Mars helicopter
Reliability Analysis of Spaceborne Electronic Components under Extreme Space Environments
abstract: The application of 6G communication systems across multiple sectors requires advanced satellite communication networks to meet the demands for high-speed transmission, low latency, and secure connectivity. The reliability of radio frequency (RF) modules, which form the core architecture of communication satellites, is critical because it directly determines the in-orbit service lifespan. This review investigates the factors influencing satellite communication systems under extreme space environments and analyzes the failure phenomena and mechanisms of 5 key spaceborne RF components: power amplifiers, frequency converters, filters, RF connectors, and antennas. In addition, it provides a comprehensive overview of current research on reliability enhancement technologies for RF modules. Both traditional and modern fault detection methods are reviewed to offer theoretical support for researchers in satellite communications and promote iterative innovation in satellite design and communication technologies. Finally, this study highlights emerging technologies aimed at improving the reliability of spaceborne electronic components and advancing intelligent fault detection. By reviewing existing studies and development trends, this study identifies future opportunities at the intersection of satellite communication technology with optical communications, artificial intelligence, and satellite recovery.

title: Absolute Navigation of High-Altitude and High-Speed Vehicles Using Relative Position Vector Measurements
abstract: Recent studies over the past few decades have indicated the utility of utilizing relative position vector information for the absolute navigation of carriers within the aerospace domain. Drawing inspiration from the principles of spacecraft formation navigation utilizing relative position vector, this paper proposes an absolute navigation method for vehicle formations. By integrating relative position vector data among vehicles, measurements from inertial navigation systems, and readings from star sensors, the method aims to accomplish navigation and positioning for high-altitude and high-speed vehicles.
