Unlike the free orbital motion of spacecraft, this work applies inertial navigation accelerometers to counteract the effects of nonconservative accelerations induced by engine thrust and aerodynamic forces. An information fusion filter based on the extended Kalman filter has been developed to estimate the motion states and sensor parameters of the aircraft. The algorithm has been tested using simulation examples, capable of achieving navigation accuracy within 200 m. A comparative simulation analysis was conducted to evaluate the effects of marked factors such as flight formation configuration, vehicle altitude, inter-aircraft spacing, and sensor noise levels. The proposed system possesses the advantages of autonomy and real-time capability, fulfilling the demand for high-precision navigation for high-altitude and high-speed vehicles.

title: Preliminary Hot-Fire Test of Ammonium Dinitramide-Based Thrusters Based on Electrical Ignition
abstract: Space sustainability and green space activities are advanced space propulsion concepts developed in the 21st century. Ammonium dinitramide (ADN)-based liquid space thrusters are typical representatives of high-performance green propulsion. To overcome the technical defects of catalytic ignition, an ADN-based thruster based on electrical ignition was innovatively designed for the first time. A preliminary hot-fire test of an ADN-based thruster was conducted using a combination of resistive ignition and arc-assisted combustion. When the thruster operated steadily at an ignition voltage of 80 V, the mean combustion chamber pressure was 0.93 MPa, the ignition delay time was 0.64 s, the combustion chamber pressure establishment time was 1.02 s, and the characteristic velocity was 1,168.7 m/s. Additionally, the average current in the decomposition area circuit was 3.3 A, and the average power was 263 W. Increasing the ignition voltage shortened the ignition delay time. The impact of the arc on the combustion and ignition response characteristics of the thruster was not important, but it could suppress pressure oscillations. Reducing the electrode spacing can shorten the ignition delay time and combustion chamber pressure establishment time. A thruster with a 0.8-mm electrode aperture exhibited better combustion and ignition response characteristics. The combustion instability in the combustion chamber is categorized as low-frequency combustion instability, and propellant decomposition instability results in combustion instability. This study provides a reference for the design and optimization of ADN-based thrusters in the future.

title: Spacecraft Proximity Operation Model-Based Sequential Coalitional Observation Game Strategy Design
abstract: To infer the mission status and threat level of noncooperative targets by obtaining their multiazimuth payload information, this paper is the first to study the problem of the spacecraft proximity operation model-based combination observation strategy design via the sequential coalitional game theory. Firstly, for the smooth switching between models, the way-point-based trajectory planning of the spacecraft is given via the Minimum Integral Square control theory, and the initial motion state solution function of the stable relative motion configuration is proposed. Based on the spacecraft relative dynamics theory, some typical spacecraft space proximity operation models, such as the drip-drop model, coplanar fly-around model, Noncoplanar fly-around model and drift-fly model, are constructed. A new sequential coalitional game algorithm of spacecraft multimodel combined observation is designed under the minimum fuel constraint, which can generate an optimal observation strategy set by constructing a game tree to select a combination of the initial motion point and the proximity operation model. Based on the combination observation strategy and the setting of the observation payload, the effective observation time of the observation spacecraft under different observation distances and field of view angles is analyzed statistically. Finally, the observation strategy set and the statistical results of effective observation time are given by simulation to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Three-Dimensional Simulations Reveal Critical Role of Impactor Shape in Kinetic Impact for Asteroid Defense
abstract: With the increasing number of confirmed near-Earth asteroids, their potential threat to Earth’s safety grows. Kinetic impact remains the most mature asteroid defense technique. To address the prevalent use of 2-dimensional models and spherical impactors in existing kinetic impact simulation researches, based on LS-DYNA software and secondary development of material models, a 3-dimensional kinetic impact simulation model was established in the context of verification with Double Asteroid Redirection Test impact. The effectiveness of the material model and geometric modeling methods was verified through momentum transfer coefficients. Three-dimensional smooth particle hydrodynamic models for 6 shapes of impactors, including sphere, cube, and cuboid, were established. It was found that the momentum transfer coefficients caused by impactors of different shapes vary by up to 29.4%. The main factor affecting momentum transfer coefficient is the aspect ratio in the envelope size of the impactor. Within the aspect ratio range of 0.35 to 2.83, momentum transfer coefficient increases with aspect ratio. However, as aspect ratio continues to increase further, β diminishes accordingly. The difference in the transverse cross-sectional shape of the impactor under the same aspect ratio only affects the shape of crater in the early excavation stage. The flat cuboid impactor produces an elliptical crater, with a maximum difference of 38% in the long and short axes, but this difference diminishes as the crater expands.

title: IncResUnet: A Model for Automatic Ionospheric Plasma Bubble Detection
abstract: Plasma bubbles are important ionospheric phenomena in the equatorial region that can cause scintillation interference in high-frequency communication. Traditional methods for detecting plasma bubbles rely on measuring the deviation of ion density over a period. However, practical applications have revealed instances of missed detections and false alarms. To address this issue, we combine the detection results of the classical method with plasma density features collected from the Formosat-1 to establish a dataset of plasma bubbles and define new identification criteria. Moreover, we introduce innovative elements into the U-Net model, creating an automated detection model called IncResUnet. Experimental results demonstrate that IncResUnet achieves an F1-score of 0.91, a recall score of 0.95, and a precision score of 0.87, outperforming traditional detection methods. Furthermore, we successfully apply the IncResUnet model, trained on Formosat-1 data, to C/NOFS data, achieving excellent detection performance and demonstrating its robust generalization capability.

title: Feasibility of Chlorella vulgaris Cultivation Using Mars In situ Resources and Human-Derived Wastes
abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of growing Chlorella vulgaris using Mars in situ resources (soil/regolith and CO 2 ) and human-derived waste streams (urine and CO 2 ). In particular, the goal was to determine the effects of cultivation media components—urine simulant, regolith extract, and CO 2 levels—on microalgal growth. Results show that the interaction of urine simulant and regolith extract significantly affected microalgal biomass productivity (MBP), with the highest MBP of 0.27 g/l-d observed in the urine-only medium, highlighting the importance of nitrogen and phosphorus. CO 2 level variations had minimal impact on MBP. Higher N and P concentrations in less diluted urine improved microalgal growth and nutrient use, emphasizing nitrogen’s critical role for high-lipid-producing species like C. vulgaris . Also, the study observed that regolith extract negatively affected MBP due to CaCO 3 formation, possibly causing cell aggregation and impaired cellular functions. However, regolith extract significantly enhanced CO 2 uptake, 10-fold higher than the urine-only medium, attributed to higher utilization of carbonic anhydrase and improved photosynthetic rate. Despite this, MBP remained lower in regolith-containing media due to simultaneous CO 2 to CaCO 3 conversion. Overall, the urine-only medium with higher initial N and P but low CO 2 levels yielded the highest O 2 production and a photosynthetic quotient of 1.04. If a higher MBP is preferred, CO 2 enrichment in the same setup is recommended. In conclusion, C. vulgaris can effectively utilize Mars resources and human-derived waste for biomass production and air revitalization, supporting sustainable life support systems for future Mars missions and long-term space habitat applications.

title: Fault Diagnosis Framework for Space TWTAs by Combining the Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model
abstract: The statistical data of space traveling-wave tube amplifier (TWTA) fault events record fault symptoms, causes, and solutions in the form of text. Effectively mining such text data can potentially enhance the reliability of devices. In this study, a fault diagnosis framework for space TWTAs is designed by combining knowledge graph and large language model. Specifically, the requirement analysis, graph retrieval, information judgment, and answer generation of the framework are all accomplished by a single large language model to enhance its stability. The knowledge graph serves as the retrieval knowledge database of the framework to enhance the professionalism. The performance of the framework is tested in practical scenarios. The results demonstrate that 92 responses are provided for 100 fault description by the framework, among which 87 responses are adopted, with an adoption rate of 94.56%. Moreover, the framework exhibits stable response consistency for the same questions and shows stability against data with noise. The performance on a larger-scale test set has slightly decreased. However, it still maintains an accuracy of 88.13%, which implies that the framework can provide effective auxiliary decision-making for fault diagnosis of devices.

title: An Error-State Kalman Filter with Multibody Integrator for State Estimation of Flexible Cable-Net Systems
abstract: The advancement of arresting cable-net recovery technology is expected to promote the application of heavy-lift reusable launch vehicles in low-cost and high-frequency space exploration. However, this process faces challenges such as insufficient or indirect measurement in complex noisy environments, as well as high complexity of the system model itself. These issues make it difficult to accurately obtain the state information of flexible arresting cables for precise control and capture of landing reusable rockets. Although the Kalman filter combined with multibody dynamics models can address state estimation in complex systems, conventional numerical integration methods often suffer from slow convergence or fail to handle the stiffness caused by strong nonlinearities and flexible effects. This study develops an error-state extended Kalman filter based on multibody integrators. The method utilizes the generalized-α method and backward differentiation formula for one-step state prediction, without model transformation or linearization of the complex nonlinear multibody system. Then, scaling and index reduction by an augmented Lagrangian formulation are carried out to improve the conditioning of the Jacobian matrix. The state prediction via the multibody integrator and an additional constraint violation correction are implemented to ensure that the estimated state remains on the constraint manifold. Simulations of state estimation performed on a flexible cable-net system model verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach. This study will provide technical support for future cable-net recovery of heavy-lift reusable launch vehicles.

title: High-Efficiency Eddy Current Detumbling of Space Targets via Dynamic Multisatellite Reconfiguration
abstract: The contactless electromagnetic detumbling method is a safe and reliable on-orbit detumbling technique for space tumbling targets. However, its efficiency substantially decreases as the relative angular velocity of the target reduces. To address this issue, this paper proposes an optimal electromagnetic detumbling method for space tumbling targets based on multisatellite collaboration. First, the influence of the relative position and orientation between a servicing satellite and the tumbling target on detumbling efficiency is analyzed, and an optimal method for generating the desired detumbling magnetic field through multisatellite formation design is proposed. Furthermore, to address the reduction in eddy current torque caused by the decay of the target’s relative angular velocity during detumbling, optimal reconstruction criteria for multisatellite formations are established. By dynamically adjusting the relative positions and orientations of the servicing satellites, the detumbling efficiency is continuously improved. Numerical simulations using a formation of 5 servicing satellites demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Results show that compared to traditional single-satellite detumbling methods, the proposed method improves detumbling efficiency by 4.68 times and markedly reduces the detumbling time.

title: Structural optimization and efficient form-finding for deployable offset ring truss mesh antennas
abstract: Abstract: The offset ring-truss mesh antenna effectively provides a large aperture and a short working focal length, while mitigating increased mass from structural height and potential signal obstruction. However, the asymmetrical geometry can adversely impact the efficiency and accuracy of the form-finding process, particularly in the application of intelligent optimization algorithms. In this paper, the form-finding process for asymmetric ring truss mesh antennas is optimized through improvements in both structural design and optimization strategy. Initially, the geometric model of the cable network is optimized by correcting the projected coordinate system and refining the configuration of the boundary cable segments, which eliminates geometric singularities and ensures a more uniform tension distribution. Additionally, a high-efficiency and high-precision shape optimization strategy is developed by integrating the strengths of the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) and Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP). This stepwise optimization approach combines the global optimization capability of NSGA-II with the high efficiency of SQP. Additionally, a numerical iteration method is used to eliminate the influence of truss deformation on the shape accuracy of the cable net. Finally, a series of numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method by comparing it with traditional approaches and geometric models.

title: Technologies and Practicing of Sampling & Encapsulating on the Moon Far Side
Space Radiation Sparks Hidden Cancer Risks: The Bystander Effect Unveiled
abstract: High-energy space radiation poses a substantial carcinogenic risk to astronauts during deep space missions. However, the mechanistic basis for this risk remains poorly defined. This study uncovers a novel oxidative stress (OS)-driven mechanism by which low-dose 56 Fe-ion exposure induces tumorigenic transformation. We demonstrate that irradiated endothelial cells (ECs) initiate a self-sustaining nuclear factor κB–tumor necrosis factor-α positive feedback cycle, which perpetuates intracellular reactive oxygen species generation and proinflammatory signaling. This positive feedback cycle not only maintains OS in irradiated ECs but also drives paracrine-mediated reactive oxygen species production and DNA damage in nontargeted bystander epithelial cells (EPs). Critically, this bystander response promotes nuclear factor κB-dependent survival signaling, including upregulation of B cell lymphoma 2, myeloid cell leukemia 1, survivin, and glycogen synthase kinase-3β, leading to tumorigenic gain of function. Crucially, we validated the tumorigenic gain of function in vivo in 8 independent mouse models with (a) nontumorigenic mammary EPs exposed 56 Fe ions or (b) cocultured with ECs exposed to 56 Fe ions; (c) directly irradiated or (d) bystander breast cancer cells cocultured with irradiated ECs; (e) nontumorigenic human bronchial EPs directly exposed to 56 Fe ion or (f) cocultured with ECs exposed to 56 Fe ion; and (g) directly irradiated or (h) bystander lung cancer cells cocultured with irradiated ECs. Tumor formation was observed in nontumorigenic mammary and bronchial EPs and heightened in cancer cell lines, confirming the transmissibility and amplification of high-energy radiation-induced OS effects. Our findings provide novel mechanistic insight into delayed effects of space radiation, highlighting OS as a central mediator of space-radiation-induced carcinogenesis, and offer a foundation for developing countermeasures for long-term cancer risks in astronauts.

title: Study on Long-Wave Resonance in High-Power Electric Propulsion Utilizing Ion Cyclotron Resonance Heating
abstract: High-power electric propulsion is expected to become the primary propulsion system in the deep space exploration due to its advantages of high specific impulse, increasing the payload ratio and reducing the flight time. Ion cyclotron resonance energization is an important method to improve specific impulse. The recently proposed ion cyclotron resonance energization under long-wavelength condition (referred as long-wave resonance) achieves most of the ion resonance, accompanied by high power absorption efficiency. The hybrid electromagnetic particle-in-cell Monte Carlo collision simulation program HYPIC is used to systematically study the effects of magnetic field, antenna, and plasma parameters on the propulsion performance. This paper summarizes the design and optimization of the long-wave resonance for high-power electric propulsion. Furthermore, since the plasma–material interaction experiments in nuclear fusion share structural similarities with high-power electric propulsion systems, this work can also provide theoretical guidance for plasma–material interaction experiments.

title: Rapid Optimization of Hovering Point for Integrated Mission of Asteroid Hovering and Landing
abstract: An asteroid landing mission usually includes 2 stages: the observation stage at a hovering point and the landing stage starting from the hovering point. To reduce the total fuel consumption of the 2-stage integrated mission, a rapid optimization method for the hovering point is developed. The optimization problem of the hovering point is established with the hovering position as the optimization variables and the total fuel consumption of the 2 stages as the performance index. To improve the efficiency of the optimization, the fuel consumption for the hovering stage is expressed as an analytical term in the performance index. Furthermore, to overcome the nonlinear problem of the analytical term caused by gravitational acceleration, a pseudo-gravitational acceleration is introduced as an augmented state. The optimization problem is solved using the sequential convex optimization method, with the landing trajectory starting from the equilibrium point as the initial value of the iteration. Finally, the optimization method for the hovering point is simulated in a hovering–landing integrated mission of the asteroid 433 Eros. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method has high efficiency in calculating the optimal hovering point.

title: The Apophis Encounter in 2029: A Rare Opportunity for Planetary Science and Defense
abstract: The 2029 close encounter of near-Earth asteroid (99942) Apophis, at approximately 38,000 km from Earth center, offers a unique opportunity to advance planetary science, defense, and public engagement. This rare event enables real-time observations of tidal effects, surface displacement, spin changes, and dust ejection, deepening our understanding of rubble-pile asteroids and improving models of their evolution. Detailed data will refine predictions of the Yarkovsky and YORP effects, enhancing asteroid dynamics research. From a planetary defense perspective, Apophis provides a critical test case for impact risk assessment and mitigation strategies, informing rapid-response reconnaissance missions. Public outreach during the event will raise awareness of asteroid science and planetary safety, fostering interest in space exploration. International collaborations, including NASA’s OSIRIS-APEX and ESA’s RAMSES missions, along with the potential contributions from China, aim to maximize scientific returns, making the 2029 Apophis flyby a milestone in global planetary exploration and defense efforts.

title: Effects of Photobiomodulation on Gut Microbiota: A Meta-analysis Based on 16S rRNA Sequencing Data
abstract: Spaceflight induces gut dysbiosis, posing health risks to astronauts. Photobiomodulation (PBM) is a countermeasure to address these complex medical issues. However, its impact on host health remains unclear due to the heterogeneity among studies. To address this, our meta-analysis systematically revealed waveband-specific effects of PBM: Infrared holistically enhanced gut microbial interaction network robustness and information transfer efficiency, while both visible light and ultraviolet enriched beneficial probiotics, particularly the Akkermansia muciniphila . Further functional analysis showed that infrared and ultraviolet exhibited distinct regulatory pathways on the gut microbiome. These findings demonstrate PBM as a noninvasive approach to mitigate space-related gut dysbiosis and support astronaut health during long-duration missions.

title: Acquisition Modeling and Optimization of Free Space Optical Link for Lunar Relay Communication
Protection Assessment Method for Advanced Whipple Shield Based on Hazardous Fragments
abstract: A Whipple shield is a dual-plate structure commonly used to protect spacecraft from space debris impacts. Upon impact, the debris strikes the outer plate, breaking into a cloud of smaller fragments with dispersed energy and momentum, reducing the likelihood of penetration through the bulkhead. However, larger and more energetic fragments in the debris cloud remain the primary threat. With advancements in high-performance materials like fiber composites, traditional Whipple shields have evolved into more advanced configurations. This study introduces a novel quantitative assessment method for evaluating the protective performance of advanced Whipple shields, using a typical-fiber-reinforced composite—carbon fiber-reinforced plastic (CFRP) laminate—as a case study. The approach integrates mesoscopic modeling with the finite-element-smoothed particle hydrodynamics adaptive method to accurately simulate debris clouds generated by aluminum spheres impacting both CFRP laminates and aluminum plates of equivalent surface density. Hazardous fragment criteria for different materials are established on the basis of these simulations. Through an analysis of fragment size, quantity, velocity, and energy angular distribution, the characteristics and lethality of debris clouds produced by aluminum impacts on CFRP laminates are evaluated. Finally, a comparative analysis of the protective performance of CFRP laminates versus aluminum plates is presented, demonstrating that CFRP laminates offer superior protection against low-velocity, small-size space debris. This assessment method is applicable to other advanced Whipple shields as well.

title: Accurate Localization Method in Multirobot Cooperative SLAM Systems under Resource Constraint
abstract: The enhancement of simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) is crucial in the evolving field of robotics, which often leads to poor trajectory localization robustness, especially under resource constraints. This study presents a relocalization method based on a historical data model and a local optimal frame-dropping strategy with a communication buffer aimed at improving the reliability and accuracy of SLAM in such challenging environments. To maintain the continuity of the back-end trajectory, the historical keyframe data were used to recalculate poses when tracking is lost. Additionally, to address data loss issues due to network unreliability, the concept of similarity measurement between frames is introduced to model the buffer problem as a local optimization issue. In real-world remote scenarios, using the Technical University of Munich public dataset as input for the SLAM’s front end demonstrates substantial improvements over the existing Centralized Collaborative Monocular SLAM algorithm, where the success rate of system tracking has increased by 4 times, and the trajectory accuracy has increased by 90.27%. These results highlight the proposed method’s effectiveness in enhancing the robustness and accuracy of trajectory localization in resource-constrained settings, marking a substantial advancement in the field of visual SLAM.

title: Space-Based Fabrication of ZBLAN Optical Fibers: A Breakthrough in Microgravity Manufacturing
abstract: ZBLAN, a heavy-metal fluoride glass fiber, achieves demonstrably better transmission in the mid-infrared range compared to silica fibers and is predicted to outperform their optical performance across the ultraviolet to mid-infrared spectrum; however, achieving this potential is hindered by crystallization during terrestrial fabrication. In this study, we leverage the microgravity environment aboard the International Space Station (ISS) to explore conditions that enable high-fidelity fiber drawing with reduced optical loss. We produced ~12 km of ZBLAN fiber on the ISS, marking the first time sufficient space-drawn material is available for comprehensive characterization. An international consortium of 5 organizations evaluated ~2.1 km length of samples with highest diameter uniformity from the produced fibers. Comparative analyses reveal that space-drawn fibers with a step-index core-and-clad structure exhibit lower optical attenuation and enhanced mechanical performance relative to their ground-based counterparts. These results demonstrate that microgravity manufacturing enables high-performance ZBLAN fiber production for near- and mid-infrared applications while opening new opportunities for advanced photonic materials in space-based industry.

title: Survey on research and development of modular reconfigurable spacecraft
Trajectory Design for Transfers from Cislunar Orbits to the Retrograde Geo-Synchronous Orbit
abstract: Retrograde geo-synchronous orbit (RGSO) possesses unique orbital characteristics and has shown great potential in space surveillance and space situational awareness. However, for various reasons, direct insertion into RGSO from the Earth is uneconomical and impractical. Thus, a novel transfer pathway from cislunar orbits to the RGSO is proposed, assuming that the spacecraft is on standby in the cislunar orbit. By selecting the distant retrograde orbit (DRO) and near rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO) as initial orbits, a transfer design method based on database search and optimization is adopted in the bicircular restricted 4-body problem (BR4BP). Both the 2-impulse and 3-impulse transfers are constructed and analyzed. Four transfer types are identified, including the direct transfer, the weak stability boundary (WSB) transfer, the lunar gravity assist (LGA) transfer, and the WSB + LGA transfer. Results indicate that for the novel transfer pathway, the propellant consumption can be kept below 1.5 km/s, regardless of the initial orbit. This provides a new possibility for deploying RGSO satellites from near-lunar space. Moreover, typical transfer types are transitioned to the ephemeris model to validate the effectiveness of the trajectory design.

title: On-Orbit Multi-Modal Intelligent Target Detection: Research Progress and Future Directions
Dual Optimization and Control of VLEO Relay Systems via Multiplexed/Classical Multimodel MPC
abstract: Very low Earth orbit (VLEO) satellites face marked challenges in downlinking large volumes of data due to short ground station contact windows. To address this, we propose a data relay multisatellite system (DRMSS). In this system, a VLEO satellite transmits data to nearby relay constellation satellites during their own ground passes. These relay satellites buffer and forward the data to ground stations during their passes, thereby extending the downlink window and improving transmission flexibility for VLEO missions. The transmitting satellite optimizes power by adjusting its attitude to maximize solar energy intake, while relay satellites aim to maximize data throughput with ground stations while maintaining alignment with the transmitter. Particle swarm optimization is used to find optimal attitude configurations due to its effectiveness in solving complex nonlinear problems within model predictive control (MPC) frameworks. To support coordinated operation, we implement an asynchronous strategy that assigns different control duties and update intervals based on satellite roles, with shorter cycles for the transmitting satellite. To address onboard computational limitations, we propose a hybrid control framework integrating traditional MPC with multiplexed MPC using asynchronous multimodel coordination. The transmitting satellite uses traditional MPC to achieve power optimization, frequent attitude maneuvers, and precise disturbance rejection. Relay satellites use multiplexed MPC to sequentially update actuator commands, marked reducing computational load while maintaining high-volume data transmission. Hardware-in-the-loop validation demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed data relay multisatellite system for supporting high-throughput VLEO missions.

title: Geometric Energy Optimized Attitude Control for Spacecraft under Multiple Attitude Constraints
abstract: As space missions grow more diverse and complex, spacecraft attitude control is required to meet multiple constraints and optimize energy consumption concurrently.To address this, this paper proposes a geometric energy optimized attitude control for spacecraft under multiple attitude constraints.The method constructs the system state space as a Riemannian manifold with a designable metric.By designing a metric tensor embedded with obstacle functions, the multiple constraints and the energy optimization objective are unified and encoded into the manifold's geometry.Consequently, the original optimal control problem is transformed into the problem of solving for a geodesic on this manifold that connects the initial and terminal states.Using Modified Rodrigues Parameters to establish the attitude dynamics and constraint models, the geometric heat flow algorithm is employed to compute this geodesic, thereby generating an attitude trajectory that meets obstacle-avoidance requirements and is energyoptimized.The results demonstrate that the geometric method outperforms both comparison algorithms.In contrast to the adaptive control approach, it achieves a reduction in energy consumption by two orders of magnitude.Compared with the Lobatto pseudospectral method, it not only reduces energy consumption by a further 5.8%, but also shortens the computation time from 35.8 seconds to 17.2 seconds, representing a 52% improvement in efficiency.

title: The Impact of Thermocapillary Convection on Phase-Change Material Melting Process under Varying Gravity Conditions
abstract: With the growing interest in phase-change materials (PCMs) for future space missions, this study investigated the melting behavior of PCMs under the influence of thermocapillary and natural convections in various gravitational environments: Earth, Moon, Mars, and the microgravity conditions of the International Space Station. Two organic PCMs with distinct Prandtl numbers, namely, succinonitrile (Pr = 23) and n -octadecane (Pr = 56), were examined as potential PCMs for application. Numerical simulations were performed in rectangular enclosures with different aspect ratios and subjected to a high imposed temperature difference, Δ T = 40 K, to simulate extreme thermal conditions. The results reveal that both gravity levels and domain geometry substantially influence flow patterns, alter the morphology of the solid–liquid interface, and affect the characteristic times of the melting process. Notably, the thermocapillary effect plays a crucial role in modulating the melting process, especially at high aspect ratios. For larger aspect ratios, thermocapillary convection dominates over natural convection, accelerating melting and altering the interface morphology. Additionally, the study demonstrates that under low-gravity conditions (such as on the Moon or Mars), the combined effects of thermocapillary and natural convections can substantially enhance the melting rate when optimized with large-aspect-ratio containers. These findings highlight the importance of the thermocapillary effect in the thermal management of PCMs under space-relevant conditions.

title: Effects of Color Labels on Visual Search Performance and Affect in a Simulated Space Station Stowage Environment: A Tianzhou-Analog Study
abstract: Visual clutter and high workload in space station cargo modules importantly impede search efficiency and adversely affect crew members’ physical and mental well-being. Mitigating visual clutter within these compartments is crucial for enhancing astronauts’ task performance and sustaining morale. This study investigated the effects of color labels on stowage bag visual search performance and affect in a simulated cargo bay environment. In a standardized laboratory study using virtual reality, 50 participants completed visual search tasks across 2 stowage conditions (organized and cluttered) and 4 color conditions, with affect assessed via questionnaire. Results indicate that color labels significantly enhance task performance and reduce negative affect in simulated cargo bay settings, with greater efficacy observed in cluttered layouts. Higher-saturation labels were found to amplify positive affect and markedly improve task performance. In summary, judicious color labels can enhance search efficiency and support psychological comfort in space station cargo bays, offering evidence-based parameters for environmental information design in dense, safety-critical storage interiors.

title: Koopman-Operator-Based Model Predictive Control of Test Mass Capturing for Drag-free Satellite
Path Planning for Mirror Assembly in Optical Detection Systems: Internal and External Parameter Optimization of Dynamic Movement Primitives
abstract: This paper proposes a hierarchical trajectory optimization method for on-orbit assembly of large-aperture optical detection systems using robotic manipulators, aiming to address the threats posed by noncooperative obstacles and mitigate the risks of module interference during assembly. The method integrates dynamic movement primitives to generate an initial trajectory and employs a hybrid optimization framework that combines intrinsic and extrinsic parameters. In the inner layer, the policy improvement with path integrals algorithm is used to optimize the shape parameters of the dynamic movement primitives, enabling the robot end-effector to pass accurately through predefined assembly points while avoiding collisions between assembled and to-be-assembled mirror modules. In the outer layer, model predictive control continuously refines the robot’s motion states, thereby enhancing the system’s ability to respond to changes in noncooperative obstacles and ensuring safe obstacle avoidance. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively ensures safe motion in dynamic, unstructured space environments and supports successful assembly operations. This study provides a well-structured and scalable path planning solution for intelligent autonomous robotic operations in complex space missions.

title: Adaptive Lunar Jumping Strategies: Understanding Temporal Associations for Behavior Consequences
abstract: More and more lunar exploration missions require robots that can adapt to the complex and unpredictable terrain of the lunar surface, where the low gravity makes quadrupedal jumping an efficient mode of movement. However, the prolonged flight phase resulting from this one-sixth Earth gravity, combined with other unchanged inertial forces, amplifies the rotational effects caused by suboptimal jumping actions and the resulting angular momentum in intricate terrains. To address the limitations of existing models in understanding the long-term consequences of sequential behavior, this paper proposes a Transformer-based reinforcement learning algorithm with causal sequence inputs to enhance jumping adaptation in complex lunar environments. A customized feature extractor for sequence input streams is designed and integrated into a reinforcement learning policy head equipped with a Transformer attention mechanism, employing a temporal window to maintain both temporal continuity and sampling randomness. Additionally, a stepwise curriculum learning framework building on the jumping and stabilization skills acquired on a plane ground is implemented, transferring to various levels of randomized rugged terrains and lunar pits of different sizes with irregular edges. This approach avoids conservative strategies and enhances training efficiency. The proposed algorithm successfully achieves efficient jumping in complex simulated lunar tasks and demonstrates superior performance compared to ablation groups across various metrics.

title: Development of surface regolith analogues of main-belt comet 133P/Elst-Pizarro
Effects and Mechanisms of Simulated Microgravity on Fusobacterium nucleatum and Multiomic Analysis
abstract: Over the years, researchers have gained deeper insights into the behavior of microorganisms under cosmic space and microgravity conditions. Microbial exposures and transmission risks for astronauts on long spaceflight differ from those on Earth. Fusobacterium nucleatum , a type of opportunistic pathogen found in the oral cavity and other mucosal sites, poses a potential threat to the control and prevention of microbial contamination in the space station. To maintain astronaut health and the cleanliness of the space station environment, it is crucial to understand the growth, biofilm formation ability, drug susceptibility, and metabolism of F. nucleatum under microgravity conditions. In our study, F. nucleatum was cultured under anaerobic simulated microgravity (ASMG) environment in a clinostat for 3 d. The control group was maintained under anaerobic normal gravity (ANG) environment for the same duration. Compared with the strain under ANG (FNN) and the original strain (FNO), the strain under ASMG (FNS) exhibited increased growth ability and biofilm formation capability, enhanced utilization of carbon sources for 3-methyl glucose, fucose, rhamnose, and d -sorbitol, increased sensitivity to sodium bromate, fusidic acid, and tetrazolium, decreased sensitivity to sodium butyrate, and distinct metabolic changes. Transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses revealed that differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) associated with adenosine triphosphate (ATP) generation, nucleotide metabolism, and glucose processing were marked up-regulated in FNS, contributing to its elevated growth. Genes and proteins linked to carbon metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis (e.g., groL , galE , and pflB ) were up-regulated, potentially supporting enhanced biofilm formation. Genes such as clpB , ylqF , grpE , nifJ , panF , and dhaL were identified as key players in regulating these phenotypic changes. To explore cross-omics regulatory coordination, we further constructed a multi-omics correlation network integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiles. Key metabolites such as trehalose, inosine, ornithine, and thiamine were found to be highly connected with genes and proteins involved in stress response, transport, and energy metabolism. For instance, trehalose displayed strong positive correlations with clpB and groL, while diaminopimelic acid showed inverse correlations with metabolic regulators, indicating a potential metabolic reprogramming under microgravity. This multi-layered network highlighted the complex, coordinated molecular response of F. nucleatum to microgravity. Overall, our study provides a comprehensive, multi-omics view of how F. nucleatum adapts to simulated microgravity at phenotypic, molecular, and metabolic levels. These findings offer novel insights into the behavior of anaerobic microorganisms in extreme environments and lay the foundation for microbial control strategies in space habitats.

title: Observing Apophis’s 2029 Flyby from Earth–Moon L2 with LUMIO
abstract: (99942) Apophis will flyby the Earth on 2029 April 13 at an unprecedented close distance. This will be a unique opportunity to study a potentially hazardous asteroid (PHA) during a close encounter with our planet. This analysis assesses whether the Lunar Meteoroid Impact Observer (LUMIO), an ESA 12U Cubesat on a quasi-halo orbit around the Earth–Moon L 2 point, can contribute to the observation of Apophis with any meaningful data. Radiometric models of the charge-coupled device (CCD) LUMIO-Cam and the environment are developed to analyze the capability of LUMIO to resolve the asteroid from the background. Sunlight reflections off the Earth and Moon are considered, as well as the noises of the detector and stray light. The geometry of the encounter is favorable for an observer placed on an orbit around the Moon, and LUMIO is indeed capable of detecting Apophis nearly a month before the flyby and of observing more than one spin rotation after it.

title: A Location-Allocation Model for Interplanetary Supply Chain Design under Operational Uncertainty
abstract: Interplanetary supply chain capability is emerging as a strategic backbone to sustain human presence beyond Earth. While technologies such as reusable launch vehicles, in situ resource utilization (ISRU), and on-orbit servicing have demonstrated feasible applications, few studies integrate these emerging technologies into a unified facility location-allocation optimization framework. This paper proposes a chance-constrained, mixed-integer nonlinear optimization model to design a multi-layer interplanetary supply chain across the Earth–Moon–Mars corridor. The model determines the strategic site and size of ISRU plants, orbital depots, and transport vehicles under demand and resource uncertainty. It further schedules propellant production, transportation, inventory holding, and backorders to minimize the total mass composed of initial launches and operations. The model incorporates 9 surface locations, 10 orbital sites, and over 120 velocity changes, accounting for orbital mechanics, energy constraint, and production–inventory imbalance. Over 40 design instances are solved and compared to demonstrate the model applicability. Baseline study shows that a 3-tier supply chain infrastructure with ISRU sited on the planets’ moons is preferred, serving Mars bases through strategically positioned depots. Numerical results show that doubling propulsion efficiency not only saves two-thirds of system mass but also reduces the infrastructure footprint. Transport vehicles with lower dry mass substantially reduce the network-wide mass and eliminate ISRU and depot footprints. This study represents a first of its kind to link space facility siting–sizing decision with chance-constrained production and demand, thereby advancing the interplanetary supply chain design theory.

title: Mission Orbit Design for the First-Ever Lunar Far-Side Sample Return Mission
abstract: The Chang’e-6 successfully performed the first-ever robotic lunar far-side sample return mission. To address the novel mission requirements for multi-object collaborative coordination during lunar surface operations, an innovative mission orbit design method, named “punctual pinpoint landing (PPL) and timed coplanar ascent (TCA) methodology”, is proposed. It is characterized by the concept of “prescheduled spatiotemporal targets” and realized by an efficient dual-loop iteration algorithm for the mission orbit design. It ensures spatiotemporal coordination among all mission participants. This facilitates the lander–ascender combination’s PPL at a predetermined landing site, the ascent module’s TCA as scheduled, and the orbiter–return module combination’s rendezvous with the ascent module at the specified time and position. To tackle the challenge of achieving convergence in the targeting solution, a dual-loop targeting method is proposed. To address the challenge of computing state-transition matrices during outer-loop iterations, a simplified iterative targeting strategy is introduced. This strategy avoids the requirement of state-transition matrix computations during the outer-loop iteration process, thereby substantially enhancing the efficiency and convergence of iteration. This method has been successfully applied to the mission orbit design of the Chang’e-6 mission. The flight results show that the method ensured the Chang’e-6 spacecraft’s PPL, TCA, scheduled rendezvous, and precise coordination with the Queqiao-2 relay satellite.

title: AI Competency Model for Aerospace Engineering Managers: A Multi-Attribute Decision-Making Approach
abstract: Against the backdrop of advancing deep-space missions such as crewed lunar exploration and Mars exploration, aerospace engineering management is accelerating the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into management workflows. Consequently, the AI competency of aerospace engineering managers has become a critical factor influencing mission delivery performance and safety compliance. This study proposes a closed-loop modeling and assessment framework for aerospace engineering management roles, based on multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) framework. First, 20 core competencies were identified through repertory grid interviews with aerospace engineering managers; subsequently, a 5-dimensional AI competency model was constructed and validated using questionnaire data (exploratory sample n = 217, validation sample n = 209). Further, an influence network relationship map (INRM) was established via decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory (DEMATEL) using expert ratings, with the DEMATEL-based analytic network process (DANP) employed to derive dimensional and feature weights. Finally, a proof-of-concept assessment was conducted on 5 genuine candidates for aerospace engineering management roles, using an improved VIKOR (VlseKriterijumska Optimizacija I Kompromisno Resenje) approach to demonstrate candidate ranking, gap diagnosis, and robustness to compromise preference settings. The proposed framework yields interpretable influence-aware weights and produces stable ranking patterns across trade-off coefficients, providing traceable decision support for mission-role readiness assessment and targeted competency strengthening under safety-critical, strongly regulated AI-enabled project environments.

title: Design and in-orbit Implement of High-precision Non-contact Micro-magnetic levitation control system
Measuring Equatorial Ionospheric Scintillation over EIA Using L-Band SAR: A Case Study
abstract: The scintillation amplitude stripes have been frequently observed in numerous equatorial nighttime acquisitions of the Advanced Land Observing Satellite Phased Array-type L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (PALSAR). This kind of artifact has been verified to be linked to the equatorial plasma bubbles, which is negative to SAR imaging and interferometry, but positive and quite beneficial to ionospheric sounding. The scintillation amplitude errors are extracted from the contaminated SAR images, which are further applied to measure ionospheric scintillation parameters based on spectral analysis. Two groups of neighboring PALSAR acquisitions in South America within a 2-h interval on the same day, suffering from visible amplitude stripes, are used for experimental validation. Both 2-dimensional (2D) and along-track 1-dimensional measurement results of ionospheric scintillation parameters are produced for this case, which shows superiority and robustness in terms of along-track resolution and observation range. The 2 total electron content crests in South America indicate the correlation with the equatorial ionization anomaly (EIA). L-band SAR can provide 2D refined imaging of equatorial ionospheric scintillation for a few minutes, especially with a high spatial resolution (better than 0.1 km) and a wide area (more than 2,700 km) in along-track. Spectral analysis based on the artifact of amplitude stripes in SAR images is sensitive to very weak ( S 4 < 0.1) and moderate (0.1 < S 4 < 0.5) ionospheric scintillation. This case captures the regional dramatic-varying structures of equatorial ionospheric scintillation, which are considered to be correlated with the equatorial ionization anomaly

title: Dynamic Analysis and Experiments on the Assembly Control of Planar Deployable Modules
abstract: On-orbit assembly via deployable modules offers a promising solution for constructing large-scale space infrastructure beyond the limitations of launch vehicle volume. This paper designs a deployable assembly module and studies the assembly control incorporating both morphing control and motion control of the module. The module consists of 3 hexagonal mechanisms connected by thin carbon-fiber shells and integrates motors, magnets, electromagnets, and nozzles to achieve deployment and docking purposes. The paper shows how to establish a rigid–flexible coupled dynamic model for the assembly module by combining the Natural Coordinate Formulation and Absolute Nodal Coordinate Formulation in the framework of arbitrary Lagrange–Euler. Then, it gives the design of proportional-derivative controllers to achieve morphing control and motion control. Both numerical simulations and ground experiments verify that the proposed control strategy can effectively reduce geometric errors and successfully complete the assembly process. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the deployable module and provide a foundation for the on-orbit assembly of modular deployable structures.

title: The Translaminar Pressure Gradient in Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome: The Relationship between Intraocular and Intracranial Pressures and Its Role in Pathogenesis
abstract: Spaceflight associated neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS) refers to the unique clinical and imaging characteristics that can develop during or following long-duration spaceflights. A number of theories about the pathogenesis of SANS have been proposed, while there is continuous interest and research about the effect of these missions on human health. The ocular translaminar pressure gradient, which is generated by the difference between intraocular pressure and retrolaminar intracranial pressure at the level of the lamina cribrosa, has been considered an important factor in the development of glaucoma and papilledema. The objective of this work is to review the changes in intraocular pressure and intracranial pressure in microgravity conditions and further discuss the role of translaminar pressure gradient in the pathogenesis of SANS.

title: EXPERIENCE OF REALITY, STRESSORS, AND NPS IN ALL-FEMALE ANALOGUE LUNAR BASE CREWS
BiLSTM-Driven Error Compensation for High-Precision Orbit Prediction with Two-Line Elements
abstract: With the rapid increase in low Earth orbit space objects, accurate orbit prediction (OP) is becoming critical for satellite safety and space environment management. Traditional physics-based OP methods, especially those relying on publicly available two-line element (TLE) data, often struggle with accuracy due to complex orbital perturbations. However, the availability of long-term, large-scale TLE datasets enables the analysis of underlying orbital error patterns. This study proposes a high-precision OP error compensation method solely based on TLE data. A bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) neural network is used to model time-varying orbital error trends and correct TLE/simplified general perturbation model 4-based predictions. Experiments on 340 low Earth orbit objects show that the BiLSTM framework effectively captures temporal error patterns, achieving an average accuracy improvement of 82% and a compensation effectiveness exceeding 94% across all targets. To assess the model’s robustness, the impact of training sample size and sampling intervals is examined, revealing that proper data configurations markedly influence compensation performance. Comparative analysis with other deep learning models (recurrent neural network, gated recurrent unit, long short-term memory, and convolutional neural network) further confirms the superior fitting and correction ability of BiLSTM. This study highlights the potential of BiLSTM networks to enhance the accuracy and reliability of TLE-based OP, providing a valuable approach for improving space situational awareness.

title: Particulate Matter Phytoremediation by Sansevieria trifasciata under a Simulated Microgravity System in a Pilot Testing Experiment: Effect of Watering and Plant Stress
abstract: Particulate matter (PM) pollution poses a profound challenge to human health and environmental sustainability, especially in extraterrestrial environments. Phytoremediation, a sustainable biotechnology, has emerged as a promising approach for air purification. This study investigates the potential of Sansevieria trifasciata to remediate PM under simulated microgravity (μG) conditions. Plants were exposed to PM in a 24-m 3 closed chamber under μG, achieved using a random positional machine. The results demonstrated that S. trifasciata maintained its PM removal capacity under μG across multiple cycles. After 16 h of exposure, the plant effectively removed PM 1 , PM 2.5 , and PM 10 , with removal efficiencies of (303 ± 41) μg/m 3 , (309 ± 54) μg/m 3 , and (353 ± 66) μg/m 3 , respectively. Notably, plant distance from the PM source did not significantly impact removal efficiency. To optimize phytoremediation, the effects of watering and plant growth regulators (auxin/IAA and gibberellic acid/GA 3 ) were examined. Watering was found to be crucial for maintaining photosynthetic efficiency (photosystem II activity), antioxidant capacity (ascorbic acid), and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, thereby enhancing PM removal. In contrast, IAA and GA 3 did not exhibit significant effects on PM phytoremediation. This study provides a foundational understanding of plant-based air purification in space environments. By leveraging the inherent capabilities of S. trifasciata , this research contributes to the development of sustainable and effective strategies for ensuring air quality in future space missions.

title: Coupling between Carotid Hemodynamics and Cerebral Blood Flow During Early Simulated Microgravity
abstract: Spaceflight microgravity induces complex cerebral blood flow (CBF) alterations, which may threaten neurological health including cognitive impairment and sensorimotor disturbances of astronauts. How CBF is regulated during microgravity, especially its coupling with carotid hemodynamics, remains poorly understood. This study investigated the coupling between acute hemodynamic changes in internal carotid and vertebral arteries (ICAs and VAs) and CBF, and evaluated the potential of ultrasound-derived parameters as portable predictors for CBF under simulated microgravity using –6° head-down tilt (HDT) bed rest (BR). Thirty-three male participants underwent Doppler ultrasound assessments of ICAs and VAs, and 3-dimensional pseudocontinuous arterial spin labeling (3D-pcASL) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), at baseline and 12 h after initiation of HDT BR. Hemodynamic parameters and regional CBF values were compared and linear regression analysis was conducted to identify predictors of changes in CBF (ΔCBF), defined as the change between 12-h HDT and baseline. Ultrasound revealed no significant changes in the bilateral ICAs. In left VA, flow velocity was significantly reduced, and right VA showed decreased resistance index, pulsatility index, and systolic/diastolic ratio. CBF significantly decreased with the most pronounced reductions in posterior circulation. ΔCBF in posterior circulation regions was associated with ultrasound parameters, and anterior circulation was predominantly predicted by baseline CBF. In summary, short-term simulated microgravity reduced CBF and this reduction was closely linked to large-vessel hemodynamic alterations, especially in the posterior circulation. These findings support the potential of ultrasound as a portable and predictive tool for early CBF assessment during spaceflight.
